[b]Dice modifiers:[/b]

Certain cards, and Hero powers change how dice behave. These effects are called dice modifiers. There are three types of dice modifiers that can appear.

Pierce: Penetrates a Defence, dealing damage even when blocked.

Reflect: Blocks an Attack and reflects it back at your opponent.

Combat is bloody and brutal. Be prepared; have good armour and cards ready to burn.

Some cards work best in combination with other cards, Rings and the right Amulet.
Armello has strong elements of chance. Find and seize every opportunity to weigh the odds in your favour.
Take unnecessary risks at your own folly, Armello is a brutal and unforgiving game of chance.
Remember to keep an eye on other Heroes' Items, Amulets, Rings, Follower and Buffs.
Experiment to find powerful combinations of Hero, Ring, Amulet and strategy.
Some Heroes are better at dealing with different situations than others, pick your battles carefully.
Manipulating King's Guards by issuing Bounties can be a great way to impede other Heroes.
Remember to make friends and allies with cards like Merchant's Agreement or Allies' Pact.
Having multiple Settlements under your control reduces the cost of Trickery cards.
Not all victory types are equal. Be open to shifting your strategy should the opportunity present itself.
The best won victories are hard fought and snatched from the claws of defeat.
The power balance in Armello can shift radically in a single turn. Never give up.
You won't win every battle and combat is often lethal in Armello. Choose your battles wisely.
The King is a mighty warrior. Carefully choose the right moment to attempt an assassination.
Completing your Quests is a powerful but long path. You don't need to finish them to win.
Use the terrain to your advantage. Mountains provide extra defence, while Forests provide Stealth at night.
Certain Spell Cards stack. Play multiple copies of Bark Skin or Evil Eye for even greater effect!

Improve your chance of success in quests by increasing your stats with cards and Amulets.

The symbols required to beat a particular Peril are the same every time it's played.
Poisoned creatures suffer -1 Health for every Action Point spent.
When slaying the King you must survive, otherwise Armello's throne will be handed to the Prestige Leader.
Corrupted Heroes gain +1 Health for every kill in battle, and +1 Rot should their victim be a Bane.

It can often be wiser to choose the safe option during your quest.
Palace Perils remain in place when failed, but are gone forever once defeated.
King's Guards will destroy any Spirit Stones they encounter.
Keeping cards moving through your hand is one of the most important skills in Armello.
In the Party of a devious enough player, the Stranger can be quite the helping hand.
Trickery Perils test Wits. Spell Perils test Spirit.
Plan your choices ahead of time. Keeping your turns short gives your opponents less time to strategise.

Execute your more insidious plays while opponents are in Battle, they won't have their eyes on the map.
There are times when buffing an enemy or debuffing yourself can be advantageous.
The first step down the Rot's dark path is Infection, but Corruption is where true power lies.
The clever adventurer explores Dungeons whilst stealthed.
Visit a Settlement on a day you're not feeling too well. You may just meet a helping paw...
More often than not, unconventional strategies win games. Get creative. Be devious.

Spirit Stones won't spawn on the same Stone Circle twice.
Perils that have had their difficulty increased will feature crossbones on their flag.
Be sure to read the descriptions cards very carefully. Haste makes for error.
With only one seat atop the throne, friendship can be a fickle thing in Armello.
After entering the Palace, play cards that grant an instant AP boost to attack the King on the same turn.
Banes are dangerous creations, manifestations of pure Rot. Don't let them infect you.
Use Teleport (Spell) or Banish (Spell) while stealthed to truly surprise your opponents.
Don't be too eager to attack. An ally is often worth more than the Prestige you'll earn from the kill.

You take up arms and decide to show your fellow bandits how it's done! Unfortunately, the beating you take only serves to embarrass you.
Yet our hero still decided to fight as an entrant! With legendary skill, <hero_name> defeated all foes, laying claim to the grand prize.
With finesse and skill, you prove you are the mightiest of all bandits, taking down the entire clan. Your prize is well-earned!
Send a proxy fighter in your stead.
And so <hero_name> selected a fine bandit warrior as their proxy fighter. They did not win, but our hero did pick up a few fighting tips!
There's little point in risking your neck when you could send another fighter in your place. They drop out early, however. A shame.
Don the Helm of Heroes
Our hero could not risk injury. They donned the Helm of Heroes and fought in the amateur bracket. They won a modest prize, but won it well.
The Battle will be fierce and you have no appetite for injury. Donning the helm, you enter, and win a lesser prize without risk.
Load the Hand Cannons
Our hero was disqualified. For some reason the Hand Cannons were banned! Still, <hero_name> was given a consolation prize.\n
You have the better equipment. Everyone you come up against is shot down. You're disqualified, but given a consolation prize.
"If only I could fight..."
Our hero noticed the Squire's will to fight. Taking pity, <hero_name> coached them on to a respectable third place.
You take pity on the squire. When the tournament begins, you coach them through the early rounds. They win third place. You take the prize.
The local bandit groups have joined together to hold a fighting tournament in your honor. Naturally you plan to win!
<hero_name> was, indeed, most flattered to learn the tournament was to be held in their honor.
Our hero had heard of a fine gathering of the mightiest bandits -- a tournament! The winner would take home a fine treasure as a prize!
Your comrades are holdin' a little fightin' tournament deep in the forest. Winner takes a mighty fine treasure, so I hear!
The Circle of Steel
Ask the Wyld to free this lost soul.
Our hero implored the Wyld to free the poor soul, but as the ghoul began to sap <hero_name>'s spirit, it was clear no help would come.
You hope the Wyld will intervene. It does not -- and the ghastly visage reaches out as you flee, its frigid claw sapping you of strength.
The Wyld's searing power purged the dungeon of the spectre's presence, leaving a glistening Spirit Stone in its place.
You hold back, letting the Wyld pierce through the fog and cleanse the dungeon of its spectre. In its place, a Spirit Stone lays.
Try to vanquish the spirit.
Our hero knew at least one way to purge a ghoul! But when their blade was drawn, the spirit disappeared in a flash. Gone, but not for good.
You draw your blade against the spirit and it seems to sense your malicious intent. It disappears in a flash, but the heavy mist persists.
Cut it down with the Moon Scythe
The spectre could not stand against the power of the Moon Scythe. The druid's gift struck the spirit down. <quest_tile> was cleansed.\n
The gleaming Wyld Steel hums as you swing in down. The spectre shrieks, it falls back, leaking magic. Magic that infuses you.
Raise the Bane's Claw
It's said the fabled Bane's Claw can draw the Rot from creatures of evil. It can. Our hero used it to force the Bane back.
The spectre shrieks. You raise the claw higher, drawing more magic. With a final cry, it flees. The magic in the claw grows stronger.
"Back creature!"
The spirit of darkness met it's match in <hero_name>'s warlock. It was banished, fleeing, never to return.
Rot magic launches from the Warlock's hands. The beast shrieks, driven further and further back. At last, it turns. Fleeing for good.
The dungeon's halls are dark, heavy with a dank mist that permeates through your fur and deep into your bones. Then, a spectre emerges!
<hero_name> wandered the dungeon's misty halls, the air growing heavier with each step. A piercing shriek revealed an oncoming spectre!
Our hero heard a rather curious rumor of a haunted dungeon hidden somewhere in Armello. Perhaps they could help clear it out?
One a' those dungeons out there is rumored to have a restless spirit haunting it. Been scaring the locals a bit -- maybe you can stop it?
The Sapping Dark
Let the Wyld be your guide.
Our hero begged the Wyld to intervene, but nothing happened. The sacrifice was carried out, and the Rot seeped through into the forest.
The Wyld ignores you, and all you hear is the scream of the poor traveler as the knife comes down. The Rot permeates the glen as you flee.
Fortunately our hero was strong with the Wyld, and the evil priest was purged of the vile Rot. The sacrifice was freed, and joined our hero.
The Wyld stops the priest, burning the knife from his paws and purging him of Rot. The grateful traveler pledges to aid you in your quest.
Slay the priest.
Our hero dashed toward the priest, cutting him down -- but sadly not before the priest's dagger pierced the poor traveler's heart.
You run the priest through, but sadly don't make it in time to save the traveler. Still, the evil priest has been stopped for good.
"Hold villan!"
By pure luck, the Apprentice failed magic subdued the priest. <hero_name> fell back laughing. The prisoner was not impressed.
The Apprentice raises a paw and fires a blast of magic. It hits a tree, bounces off to the altar, to the ground, then into the priest. Success at last!
"Move!"
Our hero couldn't move fast enough! Luckily, the spymaster could, and with a flick of the wrist, hurled and knife, wounding the priest.
A throwing knife shoots out the spymaster sleeve. It strikes the priest in the hand. He flees. The prisoner is safe, but traumatised.
Leap over!
Our hero launched into combat with the Winged Boots. The prisoner had time to flee <quest_tile> while <hero_name> did battle.
The Winged Boots let you cross to the altar before the knife falls. You tackle the priest away. The prisoner has time to escape.
You follow the ramblings of the priest and discover an altar to the Rot! The priest's knife hangs in the air above an innocent traveler!
When <hero_name> found the priest, they came upon a living sacrifice -- or rather, a poor traveler who was about to become one!
Our hero learned of a mad priest ranting and raving about in a nearby forest. With the Rot about, that could be a very bad thing indeed.
There's some kinda mad priest plying their trade out in the forest. I'd recommend shuttin' him up before he becomes too much of a problem.
The Hanging Knife
Aid the bear.
<hero_name> ventured inside and confronted the ancient Bane -- but lacked the Spirit to help. The priest perished, and our hero fled.
You follow the bear inside and are immediately set upon by a Bane! Your lack of Spirit does not help -- the bear perishes, and you flee.
<hero_name>'s strong attunement to the Wyld helped to destroy the Bane in moments! The priest, relieved, offered a treasure as thanks.
The moment you enter the manor, a Bane attacks! The Wyld aids you in slaying the beast, and the priest rewards you with a fine treasure.
Tell the priest you'll wait outside.
<hero_name> opted to hold their ground outside. The priest went ahead anyway, but the Bane inside the manor made quick work of him.
You figure it'd be safer to wait outside. This is true -- as the priest is almost immediately slain by a Bane when he goes into the manor.
Grab the Royal Shield
Within the manor, was a twisted bane. It struck with a deadly blow, but the Royal shield stopped it. The creature was soon slain.
As you enter the manor instinct causes you to raise the shield. Just in time. A strike from a bane almost shatters your arm. The bear roars.
"I'll go in first"
Our hero's fool, always first into danger, avoided a bane's attack with their legendary luck. The creature, unbalanced, was an easy kill.
The fool leaps into the manor, then screams and ducks. A bane flies over his head. Sprawling on the ground. You end it's life. Fast.\n
Detect any Rot
When the Raven's Beak Dagger shines with blood, a bane is nearby. Our hero was warned of evil's presence, and was able to defeat it.
A single glance at the Raven's Beak Dagger tells you much. It glimmers. A bane is nearby. You enter the manor, prepared and strike it down.
You meet the bear at the town gates -- they are an agent of the Wyld, they say, and they are there to purge the Rot from a nearby mansion.
Our hero decided to meet this priest, and found him to be more than a bit eccentric. Still, there was treasure in it if our hero helped!
<hero_name> received a most intriguing request: a Bear Clan priest had asked for their help to purge a Bane from a nearby manor!
Interesting contract from an interesting fellow -- some kinda bear priest is askin' for bandit help to purge a spirit from an old manor!
Exterminators of the Rot
Divine the Spirit Stone's location.
Unfortunately, our hero's wits were not quite as keen as they thought, and a deadly trap was sprung! <hero_name> lived, but only just!
You try to find the Spirit Stone, but only wind up finding a deadly trap embedded in the floor! You are gravely wounded, but escape alive.
Our hero's wits were keen by now, thankfully! The warren's traps provided no obstacle, and the Spirit Stone was soon in Bandit Clan hands!
With your wits about you, every hidden trap is bypassed with ease, letting you enter the treasure vault and claim the Spirit Stone!
Leave the stone -- look for safer baubles.
Upon seeing the bones of their lost comrades, however, our hero had second thoughts. They broke off their search, and was wiser for it.
You decide the traps are perhaps there for a reason. You break off your search to explore the warren. You earn nothing but the experience.
"There! A false wall."
The Rat Clan thinks themselves crafty and devious builders. But, as good as they think they are, they couldn't fool the Explorer.
The Explorer knows rat warrens better than their builders. With a simple push, he reveals a secret passage, towards a hidden treasure cache.

The warren echoes with ancient cries of victims long-forgotten. Many bones belong to your fellow bandits, lost in their hunt for the stone.
But our hero was not dissuaded! <hero_name> ventured forth with haste to claim the Spirit Stone and put their lost comrades to rest.
Our hero had been told of an old Spirit Stone hidden away in a Rat Clan warren lost to time. Many bandits had perished within...
Got some information about a Spirit Stone in an old Rat Clan warren. We've lost a lot of good thieves to it, though -- traps and the like.
A Stone in the Warren
Swim down and pry the Spirit Stone free.
Our hero tried to pry the stone free from its watery prison, but they lacked the strength to pry it loose -- nearly drowning in the depths!
You take a deep breath and swim down to the statue, but without the proper strength, you nearly drown trying to liberate the stone!
Our hero breathed as deeply as they could and swam down into the watery depths, prying free the stone with a mighty tug!
You dive down into the depths and, with a powerful tug, wrench the Spirit Stone free from the statue! That was almost too easy!
Search for less dangerous baubles.
Our hero was not keen diving into the dark depths, risking life and limb over a mere Spirit Stone, much as they needed it in their quest.
You decide that risking a watery grave is not the best course of action, and search the empty halls for easier treasures. You find none.
Search the lake
Our hero swam to deep, and lost themselves to the water. Luckily, the apothecary saved them, and the treasure they had recovered.
The lake is huge. You soon realise you can't make it back up in time. You awaken with the Apothecary over you, and something in your hand.
"Going underwater? Drink this!"
With the blessing of water breathing, our hero was able to search the entire lake. Sadly, the gift wore off before the stone was recovered.
A strange potion makes the air in your lungs last for hours. Thanking your Alchemist, you enter the water, and search for valuable treasures.
Swim with the Winged Boots
Our hero used the winged boots to gather treasure from the lake. Sadly, they did not let <hero_name> reach the sunken Spirit Stone.
Not just for flying, the winged boots make swimming faster as well. You're able to seize much from the lake, but don't make it to the stone.
You enter the old fortress and wind your way deep underground, soon finding the statue at the bottom of a massive underground lake.
And so <hero_name> ventured deep into an ancient underground fortress, finding the statue submerged deep underwater.
Before setting off to confront the king, our hero heard a rumor of a Spirit Stone embedded in an old Bear Clan statue.
There's an old Bear Clan statue sitting in an ancient underground fortress nearby. Rumor is, the eye is actually a Spirit Stone!
The Idol
Push yourself. Climb the peak!
<hero_name> tried to reach the mountain peak, but it was clear they lacked the strength to push on. They were forced to descend in failure.
You try to proceed up to the mountaintop, but the weather is foul and your endurance low. You are forced to descend in failure.
<hero_name> climbed the peak with ease, planting the flag in clear view of the faraway castle. It was time for the king to see what awaited.
With your legendary endurance, the mountain proves no obstacle. As you plant the flag, you glance down at the faraway castle. It is time.
Plant the flag where you are.
<hero_name> felt death's icy grip on that mountain, and decided to plant that flag where they stood. The mountain claimed it in short order.
As the deathly cold winds sap your strength, you decide to plant the flag where you stand. It is covered by snow in a matter of minutes.
"I'll go on for you."
With the journey coming to an end, the Squire finally proved themselves. They planted the flag for all to see. Truly a heroic deed.
The Squire, filled with the energy of youth, continues the climb. They plant your flag, then help you down. They'll make a fine knight.
"You can do it! You're <hero_name>!"
Bolstered by the words of the bard, our hero continued on their journey. The treacherous peak was overcome. All Armello saw the flag.
The bard's words urge you on. Step after freezing step. At last, you reach the peak. The bard is right. You are mighty.
"Take this! Go on!"
The blacksmith gave our hero their greatest secret. A legendary everflame. The eternal fire warmed our hero, letting them continue on.
The blacksmith hands you the secret of his trade. An everflame, used to start the forge. It's warmth lets you finish the journey.
Your climb up <quest_tile> is long and precarious -- it tests your very being as the cold wind and ice whip over you.
Our hero struggled up the peak, its icy wind chilling them to the bone straight away. This trek could be their last if they weren't careful!
<hero_name> knew it was time to declare all of Armello under Bandit Clan protection. A Bandit Clan flag on its highest peak would do.
It's time to declared your intent to the king. That mountain peak is visible from the castle wall -- plant our flag where they can see it!
The Coat of Arms
Sneak in. Force open the vault.
<hero_name>'s fellow bandits had bribed the guards in advance, but the vault door required strength far beyond them to open. What a waste!
Your bandits have bribed the guards, but the vault door cannot be reasoned with. You try to open it, but lack the strength to even budge it!
The guards had been bribed, so the vault door was the only challenge. <hero_name> pulled it open with ease and claimed the treasure within!
Your fellow bandits have bribed the guards in advance, and in mere minutes you've forced open the vault and made off with its treasures!
Have your fellow bandits help.
<hero_name>'s bandits opened the vault with ease... but also made off with the treasures worth taking! So much for honor among thieves!
With your bandits by your side, the door is an easy hurdle. Alas, your comrades make off with the choicest treasures, leaving you nothing.
"I've broken into better."
<hero_name>'s Spymaster had robbed more secure vaults than she'd had hot meals. The theft was easy, and they split the loot.
You defer to the Spymaster, who plans a daring heist. Although you seem to be little more than a distraction, you agree and split the loot.
Sneak in with the Mirror Cape
Though the vault was too great a challenge, many treasures were undefended. Using the mirror cape, our hero was able to collect them.
Under cover of dark, none spot the telltale shimmer of the cape. Under it's protection, you sneak into the building. Simple.
Talk your way in
The shifting shadows around the Masquerade Mask gave our hero unnatural grace. They talked their way into the building, and back out.
The guard's eyes glaze over at the mask's sight. Its strange enchantments let you talk your way into a few rooms, and steal a few treasures.
You enter the unassuming town and quickly find the vault inside an unassuming but very well-protected stone building. This will be tricky.
<hero_name> entered the town and discovered the vault was quite a bit more imposing than originally thought. How would they open it?
The Bandit Clan's intelligence had learned a most useful fact: the location of the king's treasure vault!
It's taken some doing, but we've learned where the king's keeping a vault full of his most valued treasures. A small town nearby!
The King's Vault
Negotiate. Save yourself!
<hero_name> tried to convince the chief to ally with the bandits. The negotiations fell through -- right when our hero fell from the tree.
You try to convince the squirrel chieftain that you're a trustworthy sort, but he isn't convinced -- and pushes you right out of the tree.
It was only through <hero_name>'s clever negotiation that a long-lasting alliance between the bandits and the squirrel tribes was sealed.
You make a compelling case to the squirrel chieftain and he agrees to your terms -- even throwing in a follower's card to sweeten the deal!
Abandon the negotiations with speed.
Our hero realized in a very short matter of time that the squirrels would not negotiate. <hero_name> quickly broke off the talks and fled.
You can tell when you're wasting your time, and also when your life is in peril. This situation encompasses both -- so you beat a retreat.
Plant the Royal Banner
Impressed by our hero's tenacity, and their fury at the Mad King, the squirrels let <hero_name> go, and gave him a token of good faith.
The squirrels sneer, then gasp as you spit on the King's symbol. "You may hate me. But I'll wager you hate the Mad King more."
"We can work this out."
<hero_name> kept their head by the skin of their teeth. The trader negotiated release, and cooperation against the Mad King.
The trader steps forwards, paws raised in peace. "I'm sure you want something. No blood need be shed." The squirrel's chief smiles.
"Gold. Freedom for Gold."
The coin master spoke, stumbling over his words. It was the promise of imaginary gold that keept our hero's head on their shoulders, and off a pike.
Your coin master steps forward. He negotiates, wagering your life against squirrel greed. Greed wins out. Thank the Wyld. You're safe.
You are led to the chieftain's hut by spearpoint. There he insists your head is more valuable on a pike as a warning than on your shoulders!
<hero_name> allowed themselves to be led by spearpoint to the old grump of a chieftain. Our hero was in grave danger, surrounded by steel.
Our hero had heard tales of a long-lost tribe of squirrel warriors hidden in the woods. Their skills could be of help in taking the throne!
Those woods are dangerous, my friend -- but they're also renowned to conceal a tribe of ancient squirrel warriors. They could be of help!
Treaty of the Trees
"This traveller is under my protection."
<hero_name> lied to the trio, explaining the traveler was under their protection. Sadly this only led to them waylaying our hero instead!
You try to explain to the trio that the traveler is under your protection, but this simply leads to them knocking you unconscious. Oops.
The traveler, our hero said, was under Bandit Clan protection. The thieves fled, and the treasure hunter offered a fine reward as thanks.
You tell the trio that the traveler is with you, and they wisely back off. As thanks, the treasure hunter offers you part of his haul!
Leave the traveler to his fate.
<hero_name>, clearly outnumbered, backed off. The traveler would perish, their treasure to be stolen. But our hero made it out just fine.
Three of them, one of you. Best to let fate handle this one. As you walk away, you can hear the traveler's screams carry on the wind.
Save her!
The thieves were overcome thanks to the armor granted by the lionheart breastplate. The treasure hunter, split the loot with <hero_name>.
The Lionheart Breastplate clicks into place. The battle is furious, but every strike you fail to parry clangs off your armour. You win.
Cut them down
Cursed steel. Unstoppable dark power. The Bane's Blade was a weapon of Rot, and our hero used it to slay the thieves.
The thieves terror as you draw the Bane's Blade pleases you. You cut them down, then split the treasure with the terrified traveler.
"Charge!"
The problem with being a murderous thief, is that sooner or later you find someone more murderous. <hero_name>'s berserker, was that someone.
Your berserker bellows and bull rushes the thieves. Those that don't scatter are crushed before his mighty charge.
You follow the rumor to a large field in an ancient plain; and quickly discover the treasure hunter held hostage by three murdering thieves!
Our hero followed a rumor that a traveler had cracked the riddle -- and they had! But a trio of villains was holding her hostage for it!
Many generations ago, Felsin'rah, the feline treasure hunter, hid a grand haul behind a riddle none could solve. Until now!
Hear rumors that a traveler's finally cracked the Riddle of Felsin'rah, the crazed treasure hunter! Maybe you can liberate some of it?
The Treasure of Felsin'rah
Disarm this Wolf Clan warrior.
Our hero thought they would try and send the warrior back with a message -- instead, the wolf beat them mercilessly, forcing them to flee.
You'd rather send this pup back to the king with a warning, but he proves a most worthy opponent. You take quite a beating before you flee.
Our hero bested the warrior in a matter of moments, then sent them crawling back to the king with a simple, short message: "Soon."
With skills honed over a lifetime, the sentinel stands no chance. You disarm him, and send him back to the king with a message: "Soon."
Slay this forest sentinel where he stands.
Our hero had no time for these trivial obstacles -- the king's own madness would prove obstacle enough! They slew the wolf and moved on.
This wolf is merely another obstacle in your path to the king -- and all obstacles can be removed. You slay the sentinel and move on.
"You can't catch us both!"
Wolves aren't the brightest of creatures. Our hero and the Brilliant Fool out maneuvered him. He returned to the king an embarrassed failure.
You fool takes off to the left, as you dart right. The foolish wolf twists back and forth confused, hesitant. You outrun him with ease, laughing.
Force the Wolf to flee
The wolf grew slowly deranged with pain as our hero tortured it with the Poppet. At last, it ran, terrified. Our hero could pass freely.
Hidden within the nearby trees, you attune the poppet to the wolf. Bit by bit, you torture it, until at last, whimpering, the wolf flees.
Approach and Attack
Strike after strike was blocked by the Royal Shield. Our hero slew the wolf. The king could fight them in person soon enough.
Head hidden behind the Royal Shield, you approach the assassin. His blows are easy to block, and as he stumbles, you cut him down.
The Wolf Clan warrior in question turns out to be a representative of the king. An assassin, more like, sent to impede your path the throne.
The warrior appeared to be in the employ of the royal court, sent to stop <hero_name> from getting any closer to the king's throne!
A strange Wolf Clan warrior had been causing trouble in a nearby wood under Bandit Clan protection. Our hero decided to investigate.
Travelers under our protection are sayin' there's a Wolf Clan warrior blockin' their path through the wood. You'd best sort out this mess.
The Forest Sentinel
Slay the quartet!
Our hero couldn't stand idly by, but their combat skills were no match for the four killers. Our hero barely escaped. The loyalist didn't.
You charge into the torture chamber, but the royal assassins are renowned for their brutality. You earn a few new scars before fleeing.
Our hero charged into the torture chamber, slaying all four assassins in a matter of moments. The loyalist was, thankfully, still alive.
You introduce yourself at the point of your blade, slaying the quartet and freeing the poor loyalist, who offers to aid you in your quest!
Fetch help from your fellow bandits.
Our hero hurried away to fetch aid from the Bandit Clan, cornering the assassins and ending their lives. The loyalist, though, did not last.
You run back to your comrades and order them to help, but the loyalist is dead when you return. At least the assassins pay for their crimes.
"I'll save him!"
The apprentice's magic almost got <hero_name> killed. Thankfully, it provided cover to free the loyalist, but weakened him as well.
The apprentice casts a spell that fills the dungeon with choking mist. "Oops." You stagger through it and free the loyalist. Cursing.
Strike with the Moon Scythe
The loyalist was saved through perfect skill with the moon scythe. Almost perfect. A stray blow cut them. They could not join our hero.
The confined space of the dungeon means nobody has room to escape. You slash in great arcing blows, striking down the assassins.
Charge!
Our hero leapt to battle, slaying the King's Assassins. Though they had time to wound the loyalist, our hero had still saved a life.
The Helm of Heroes blocks a strike that would have crushed your skull. The assassins fall, though they have time to wound the loyalist.
You follow a solitary scream down into the depths of the dungeon, finding a quartet of royal assassins torturing a Bandit Clan loyalist!
When our hero arrived, they found a Bandit Clan loyalist was being tortured deep within by the four mad creatures.
<hero_name> learned that a quartet of royal assassins, the vile edge of the king's blade of tyranny, was holed up in a nearby dungeon.
There's an old dungeon a good ways from here that the king's royal assassins are using as a base. Perhaps it's time you disbanded them?
The Vile Quartet
Slay the King's Guard and free the village.
Our hero tried to liberate the village through force, but the soldiers outnumbered our hero. Wounded and near death, they fled the quarry.
You rush to the quarry, blade swinging. The King's Guard, however, is well-trained and outnumber you ten to one. You flee with dire wounds.
They leapt forward, their blade cutting down the soldiers and freeing the poor townsfolk. <hero_name> had proven themselves a worthy hero!
Your blade makes quick work of the soldiers, and the townsfolk even pitch in to help! Finally free, they give you a fine treasure as thanks.
Help liberate the townsfolk.
It was best to avoid fighting the soldiers single-handedly -- so our hero pressed the townsfolk to fight. Many died, but the soldiers fled!
You sneak past the soldiers and help arm the townsfolk for rebellion. The ensuing battle costs many lives, and the remaining soldiers flee.
"A smokescreen should let them escape!"
The guards watched helplessly as the prisoners fled through a smokescreen created by <hero_name>'s conjurer. The villagers were saved.
After a few moments mumbling, the Conjurer causes a plume of smoke to explode into the air. The chaos lets the villagers escape.
Show the Royal Pardon
The Royal Pardon forced the guard's hands. They grudgingly let the villagers go free. They threw up their pickaxes in joy.
The guards raise their weapons as you approach. "These are free beasts!" You cry. The guards are forced to let the villagers go.
You find the village devoid of townsfolk -- everyone is in a nearby quarry, slaving away over rocks with pickaxes as the soldiers look on.
<hero_name> prepared for battle, traveling with speed to the village quarry. There, creatures young and old toiled under the soldiers' eyes.
<hero_name> learned of a dire situation nearby: a village enslaved by the King's Guard! Could our hero free them from the king's madness?
A nearby village is being pressed into servitude by the King's Guard. They're beggin' for help -- ain't no reason that help can't be you.
Settlement Under Siege
Use the Wyld as your shield.
<hero_name> tried to use the Wyld to defeat the Bane, but the Wyld would not offer its aid. Our hero was corrupted by the Rot as they fled.
You beg the Wyld to protect you... but nothing comes of it! You feel the Bane's corrupting force flow through you as you flee the dungeon.
<hero_name> raised a hand, and the Wyld answered. The Bane exploded in a magnificent fireball, purging it from that dark place forever.
You are an agent of the Wyld, and the Wyld is your shield in the darkness. The Bane explodes in a fireball, and you claim the Spirit Stone.
Fight the Bane!
<hero_name> drew their weapon and slew the Bane. Alas, its dark powers collapsed the ancient tunnels, trapping the Spirit Stone within.
You draw your weapon and do battle with the Bane. When you slay it, the tunnel begins to collapse, forcing you to flee without the stone.
"Back foul monster!"
Our hero's warlock forced back the Bane before it could harm <hero_name>. Unfortunately, the creature fled with the spirit stone.
The warlock's words ring with the power of Rot. The Bane, terrified, shrieks and flees, but takes the stone with it.
Raise the Wyld Talisman
Our hero used the power of the Wyld Talisman to force the creature back. It's cries of pain can still be heard in the dungeon today.
The Bane shrieks as if you held the very sun. It grabs the stone and flees, but you feel the talisman infused with stronger magic.
Absorb the Bane's Power
The Bane's feathers and skin drew into the Bane's Claw like torn cloth. Our hero felt no guilt. The beast earned its terrible fate.
The Bane falls apart as you raise the claw, its power sapped away. It manages to smash the spirit stone before you totally absorb it.
You enter the dungeon and, among the old bones of explorers long perished, you find the Spirit Stone... and a vile Bane!
So our hero ventured into those darkened halls. Among the many bones, the priest's Spirit Stone lay. Then, a piercing screech! A Bane!
<hero_name> heard a rumor of an old Bear Clan priest venturing into a dungeon with a Spirit Stone... and never reappearing!
A Bear Clan priest went into that dungeon a little while ago, carryin' a Spirit Stone. Nobody's seen 'em since. Maybe it's still down there?
The Bear's Bane
Ask the Wyld to spare this poor soul.
Surely the Wyld would help this innocent creature! Alas, it did not, and our hero was touched by the Rot before being forced to flee.
The Wyld seems to scoff at the enormity of your request, doing nothing but drawing the creature to you. The Rot grips you, and you flee.
Surely the Wyld would help this creature! A healing light filled the swamp, purging the darkness and freeing the traveler of their madness.
The swamp fills with light, clearing the Rot and freeing the traveler of his affliction. Relieved, they offer to aid you in your quest!
Slay the creature. Their time has come.
It was already too late for them, our hero realized. They slew the poor creature, its final screams a symphony of pain and suffering.
You approach the creature, weapon drawn. The battle is quick, and the poor soul's howls of pain echo in your ears for all time.
Put the beast down
Our hero raised the Hand Cannons, ending the corrupted beast's life. <hero_name> buried the body. A final honor to its spirit.
A single shot from the Hand Cannons does the job. The beast makes no sounds as it falls. Rot leaks off the fallen body.
Purge the Creature
Green fire purged the foul beast. The Wyldfyre staff would not stomach evil lingering in <quest_tile>.
Green flames launch from the Wyldfyre Staff, burning the rot from the creature's flesh. It perishes. <quest_tile> is free of evil.
Deep in this gloomy mire you find the source of the Rot -- a lost traveler strong in spirit but corrupted beyond all hope.
The old swamp was coursing with Rot, like blood through a vein. There, in the center, a poor traveler stood corrupted by the foul force.
<hero_name> knew that before they took the throne, the Rot in Armello needed to be stemmed. Fortunately, a wellspring had been found.
Before you go after the king, I hear there's a wellspring of Rot in a swamp feeding the evil in this land. Do what's right -- destroy it.
The Deepest of Rot
Enter the circle and ask for a blessing.
Our hero stepped inside the circle, but was greeted with naught but pain. Their spirit was weakened, driving them from the circle.
The moment you enter, you feel weak. Then there is pain. You can't even finish your request before you are forced from the circle.
Our hero stepped forth, and the Wyld responded with a powerful burst of healing light. There, in the center of the circle, a grand treasure.
The moment you enter, there is a powerful warmth -- the Wyld approves your quest! A grand treasure materializes before your very eyes.
Enter the circle and ask for enlightenment.
Our hero knew better than to ask favours of the Wyld, instead deciding to seek advice. The Wyld responded, offering a gift of spirit.
You decide against asking for trinkets, and instead ask the Wyld to aid you in understanding. It complies, and you leave feeling wiser.
"There are ways, to trick the Wyld."
The stranger knows the way of the Wyld and the Rot, and how to trick them both. our hero received a blessing... somewhat.
The Stranger takes your paw, walking in with you at the same time. Together, you are worthy, and receive half a blessing each.
You stand before the ancient stone circle, feeling the power of the Wyld all around you. If you wanted a blessing, this would be the place.
So they traveled to a stone circle, drawn by an ancient power that no creature in Armello truly understood. What awaited them within?
<hero_name> knew that before facing their final test, a blessing from the forces of the Wyld would be a good idea.
Before you go after the king, might be a good idea to get a blessing from the Druids. Or the Wyld. Or, y'know, anything that can help.
A Gift from Above
Pick the lock and enter the castle.
Our hero's thieving skills paired well with Vorak's brilliant lockpick, and the castle gate stood no chance. Ahead, the king awaited.
The lock's tumblers spin and roll into place, standing little chance against Vorak's craftsmanship. The gate opens, and the king awaits.
You take up the expertly-crafted pick and, with intelligence gathered by your spies and fellow bandits, quickly find the locked castle gate.
Our hero took up this most brilliant of thieving tools and quickly set about to find a lock worthy of its craftsmanship: the castle gate.
Vorak, most famous of all bandit locksmiths, delivered to our hero a simple pinewood box. Inside: the most magnificent lockpick ever built.
Old Vorak says he's finally done it -- made the perfect lockpick. He's asking to meet you.. says it should get you into the castle.
Vorak's Key
Charge!
Our hero charged, ready to fight. But the challenge would prove too much for <hero_name>. They were injured, and forced to flee.
You march into the dungeon. With hindsight, you overestimated your power. The Bane leaps to attack, and you're forced to desperately flee.
The Rot beasts of Armello were not ready for someone of <hero_name>'s power. Our hero cut the Bane down, the first victory of many to come.
As soon as you step inside, the Bane leaps from the shadows. You're ready! You fell the foul beast, then leave. You have a bounty to claim.
Block off the dungeon
Rather than face the beast, <hero_name> locked it inside the dungeon. Safety and wisdom over brute force. A good choice for a future ruler.
Safety is more important than a bounty. You block the Bane inside the dungeon. You'll not let this creature take innocent lives.
You can smell Rot from <quest_tile>'s entrance.  The Bane seems well entrenched. Perhaps this was a tad ambitious.
The beast had clearly been lurking in the dungeon for many moons. <hero_name> would need to proceed carefully.
<hero_name> took up a bounty for the slaying of restless banes. A particularly troubling creature was lying low in <quest_tile>.
A bounty has been offered to wandering heroes. Spirit Stones for Bane skulls. The first target is hiding in a nearby dungeon.
Old Ways
Attack the caravan
The slavers were tougher than <hero_name> thought. Although victorious, the prison caravan escaped. Our hero's first failure stung.
Soldiers pour out. The caravan peels away. Although you defeat the onslaught of rats, the prisoners are gone by the time the battle ends.
The battle was quick. With the slaves free, and a new companion in tow, <hero_name> had taken a strong first step in their quest.
Rat guards are no match for a trained warrior. You dispatch them. The prisoners cheer your name. One swears to your cause as thanks.
Alert the King's Guard
Biding their time, our hero stalked the caravan across the plains, then called in the king's guard to help assault it.
When the caravan stops for the night, you alert the guards of the nearest settlement. They rush the slaver camp with you, and free the prisoners.
Staring across <quest_tile>'s endless fields, you spot the caravan weaving through the grass. Time to teach these slavers a lesson.
Our hero found the scoundrels moving their caravan across the plains. It was time to start making a difference in Armello.
Treacherous slavers were moving prisoners across <quest_tile>. <hero_name> could not let their dark trade continue.
Rat kidnappers have been moving their prisoners across Armello to sell as slaves.
Rat-road
Slay the beast!
The beast had no appetite for a proper confrontation. It dealt a glancing blow and fled. The wound seemed affected in some way.
You turn, howl, and scan the trees. The beast flashes past, nicking you with a claw, before vanishing. The wound is small, but feels tender.
The beast was defeated with ease. <hero_name> had taken the first step in their quest, and had a treasure to show for it.
The beast is hidden in the brush behind you. It shrieks as you charge. You bring it down in a hail of blows. You find the artifact in its lair nearby.
Scare the beast away
The creature was too dangerous to face head on. <hero_name> escaped into the trees, living to fight another day.
With great care, you do battle with the beast. Afraid of a real challenge, it hisses and flees, taking it's treasure with it.
The forest seems denser than you remember. Forcing through the thicket you freeze as you sense the creature's eyes upon you.
As our hero struggled through the thick forest branches, they felt the Rot beast's cold eyes watching them from the shadows.
<hero_name> heard rumour of a rot beast roaming <quest_tile>. Supposedly it had killed a courier carrying a valuable treasure.
A courier carrying a great artifact has been killed by a rot beast. The King's Guard declared the beast's killer can keep the treasure.
Rogue Beasts
Set up a harness and scale the outcrop
Our hero's harnesses were not up to the strain of the mountain. <hero_name> fell, only just avoiding the plummet into the ravine.
Halfway up the outcrop, your harness snaps. You catch yourself on the ledge, but the stone slips down the mountain. Lost forever.
The climb was no challenge for <hero_name>. Our hero had tasted their first victory. The throne of Armello would be soon to come.
Hand over hand, loose rock over loose rock, you haul yourself up the outcrop, and seize the stone. You swing down on the harness. Perfect.
Mark the spot for other Bears
The stone was out of <hero_name>'s grasp, but a ruler can't think for personal glory. Our hero marked the spot for other Bears to find.
The stone might be out of your reach, but you'll be damned if you let it fall into Rat Clan hands. You map the spot for other bears.
The mountain is mercifully calm. You find the spirit stone balanced on an outcrop over a ravine. It will be a difficult climb.
For once, no storm was ravaging the mountain. The journey up was easy, but the stone itself would need an experienced climber to reach.
<hero_name> heard rumour of an ancient and powerful spirit stone, spotted high up on <quest_tile>.
A Spirit Stone has been sighted high on a mountain peak. Any bear brave enough to climb up is welcome to it.
High Peril
Mediate the Argument
Our hero's good intentions were taken advantage of. The stranger ran and <hero_name> was forced to settle his debt with the stall owner.
You call out. The stall owner glances over but the stranger uses the distraction to escape. You are forced to pay for the broken urn.
<hero_name> solved the petty argument by paying the stranger's debt. In thanks, they offered our hero assistance in their quest.
You defuse the situation before the pair come to blows. The stranger has no money, and offers to join you if you cover their debt.
Separate the two
Our hero stopped the situation before it turned violent. The rot had made Armello's citizens quick to anger.
You step between the two figures and keep them apart. You order them to leave. Whoever's at fault, violence is never the answer.
As you enter the market at <quest_tile> you notice a stall owner in a violent argument over a smashed urn with a passer by.
The sounds of the market assaulted <hero_name>'s ears. Among them, was a heated argument between a stall owner and a passer by.
<hero_name> began a journey to <quest_tile>. The grand market taking place there would outfit our hero for their quest.
A nearby village is hosting a grand market. You'll surely be able to find supplies for your quest there.
Paid Labour
Pick a culturally important site.
<hero_name> searched every site they knew was important to the deer folk, but after several hours, admitted failure.
Your rack your brains, and check every site that you know as significant. Hours of exhausting search later. Nothing.
Thanks to their love for children's tales, <hero_name> found the site where the treasure had been buried, and unearthed it.
A line from a fairy tale about a wandering doe, leads you to a nearby river. Buried at the bank you find the treasure you were looking for.
Search for ancient areas
Unfortunately, the treasure would remain lost. Still, the day's work reminded <hero_name> of part's Armello's history they had forgotten.
It's as good a hope as any. You give up after a few hours search. You resolve to pay more attention to history books in future.
<quest_tile> seems to go on forever. There's no hint where the treasure is, or where to start looking.
Unfortunately for <hero_name>, <quest_tile>'s grasses extend for miles, and there was no clue where the treasure might be.
<hero_name> heard stories of a fabled treasure in <quest_tile> hidden away by the strange deer folk many years ago.
Stories tell of a buried treasure, hidden by wandering deer druids many years ago. It would be useful in usurping the Mad King.
Buried Treasure
Let the vision play out
The vision was not of good fortune. <hero_name>'s quest seemed cursed. Would our hero succumb to the morbid predictions?
Pictures flash past. The Mad King on his throne. The land gripped by rot. Pain. Death. You collapse. Trembling. This does not bode well.
<hero_name>'s journey was clearly blessed by the Wyld. When the vision faded, they were left with a gift.
The vision is of hardship, and dire peril. But at journey's end, a chance at peace. You feel the cold of a Spirit Stone appear in your hand.
Close your eyes. Ignore the vision.
Rather than suffer at the fickle hand of the Wyld <hero_name> rejected the vision. The throne awaited, there was no time for weakness.
Pain and weakness is not a good way to start a journey. You close your eyes and force the vision from your head. You'll make your own path.
You kneel before the ancients stones, praying for guidance in the journey ahead. Your eyes cloud over. A painful vision forms.
The stones welcomed <hero_name>'s prayers. They blessed our hero with a strange vision.
Before our hero's quest could begin, <hero_name> decided to journey to <quest_tile> to pray to the Wyld.
Tradition dictates that Armellians pray at a stone circle before embarking on any great quest.
The Right Way
Reach into the pool
The Wyld Pool judged <hero_name> as wanting. It drained them of their strength. An ill omen for the quest.
Cold. Ice cold. The chill races up your arm. You rear back. A terrifying voice echoes in the air. A poor judgment. You feel weakened.
The Wyld pool judged <hero_name> as worthy. It gifted them with a treasure. A strong first step in their quest for the throne.
Warmth. Blissful warm. The pool soothes your body. You hand closes around something. You draw it out. A treasure!
Offer a prayer and leave
Rather than bother the Wyld with trivial questions <hero_name> offered a prayer. Perhaps they would return at the journey's end.
<hero_name> was modest. It was presumptuous to undergo the judgment when there was still work to be done.
The Wyld pool sits. Its calm water glistening. To be judged, one must simply reach inside. Doubt rushes through you. Is it worth the risk?
<hero_name> arrived at the Wyld pool. It's cool waters beckoned our hero's approach. But they were filled with doubt.
<hero_name>  journeyed towards <quest_tile>. Within its trees, a sacred pool was said to bless the worthy with treasure.
A mysterious "Wyld-pool" in the depths of a forest is said to bestow treasure on worthy heroes.
Wyld Pool
Restore their faith in the Wyld
The heathens would not listen. Perhaps <hero_name> had too much hope in Armello. The rot had taken a terrible toll on its inhabitants.
You approach and preach the way of the Wyld. The heretics laugh. Even you feel your words fall flat. The bandits jeer as you leave.
Although it seemed <hero_name>'s words fell on deaf ears, one heretic left and swore fealty to our hero.
Most of the heretics are unwilling to listen, but one seems doubtful. That night, the convert steals away and swears fealty to you.
Call the Wyld down on the camp
<hero_name> would not let heresy stand. Our hero demonstrated the Wyld's power, by tearing the heathen camp apart.
False magic and trickery has no power against the true Wyld. You unleash the wyld's fury, destroying the camp.
Arriving in the depths of <quest_tile> you come across the group's campground hidden in the mist.
The heretics were hidden deep within <quest_tile>. <hero_name> found their camp and made preparations.
<hero_name> heard of a heretic group dabbling in magic that was twisting the Wyld. It was this kind of treachery that spread the Rot.
A group of heretics have forsaken the Wyld. They're hiding in a nearby forest, using dark Rot magic to gain power.
Heretics
Hold fast and wait for the perfect moment...
After a quick struggle, <hero_name> defeated the killer of <quest_tile>, though they did not come out unscathed.
You try to hold your ground, but the crazed killer's erratic movements throw you off guard. You emerge victorious, but wounded.
But <hero_name> wasted no time felling them. With the stones cleansed, a grateful <test_reward> joined <hero_name>'s adventure.
You time your strike perfectly, slaying the mad killer. A stranger approaches and swears fealty to you for avenging their fallen partner.
Charge!
<hero_name> exploded into a charge and the awesome might of the Bear Clan rained down upon the crazed killer, literally crushing the taint.
You charge -- and while the killer is deft, they are no match for the sheer strength and size of a full grown bear. Few are.
The Bane's Blade flashes
The Bane's Blade cut the madman down. <hero_name>was troubled. Was the blade's power truly worth the darkness it held?
Your cursed sword moves of its own accord. Two slashes and the madman falls. You're troubled, but still search the body for useful tools.
"Stand aside <hero_name>!"
<hero_name>'s mighty companion slew the madman before he could harm our hero. The taint had been purged.
Your berserker charges forward. The madman has no chance. He's slain, and his body yields a small reward.
Don your armour
Our hero was prepared for the fumbling attacks of untrained slavers. Sliding on their Helm of Heroes, <hero_name> attacked with bear's fury.
You reach the village square just as the slavers spring their ambush. You slide on the Helm of Heroes and attack. This will be over quickly.
When you arrive, two figures appear in a brilliant flash of light. One is slain by the other in a short moment, and the killer charges you!
Arriving at the standing stones of <quest_tile>, <hero_name> is witness to murder. The killer wasted no time rushing our hero...
Our hero had little to go on, but the words 'dark taint' certainly piqued their interest and so to <quest_tile> they went.
Some of the local elders are saying a dark taint haunts a Stone Circle not too far from here.
A Date with Destiny\n
Combine your strength with the Wyld.
Our hero summoned all available strength, relying on the Wyld for support, but the magic proved too strong. The mage was never seen again.
You summon your strength, supporting yourself with the healing call of the Wyld. But the magic proves too much, and you relent in failure.
Our hero destroyed the magical barrier with ease, freeing the trapped mage within. No more would the Rot meddle with this powerful mage!
You destroy the barrier with your incredible strength, freeing the grateful mage. Cultists of the Rot had trapped him, fearful of his power.
Find fellow members of the Bear Clan for aid.
Instead, our hero turned to others in the Bear Clan for aid. Unfortunately, the slow speed of their action seals the mage's untimely demise.
You leave the mage's home and search out fellow Bear Clan acolytes -- unfortunately, by the time the barrier is destroyed, the mage is dead.
The Wyldfye Staff glows with an odd light...
<hero_name> held the ancient staff to the barrier, and the shriek of the dying Rot filled the air. The mage was freed, our hero victorious!
You hold the staff aloft, its arcane magic freeing the mage from the dastardly magic. Cultists of the Rot stand no chance against the Wyld!
"These things don't work on me."
The stranger leapt to our hero's aid, and helped free the trapped wizard from his magical prison. Treachery was stalled, and a mage made safe.
Eyes wide, the stranger steps through the barricade. You stare, shocked. He's able to assist the mage, and splits his reward with you.
Use the Rot to break through
<hero_name> was forced to embrace the power of the Rot to free the trapped mage. The Raven Beak dagger shattered the strange barrier.
You rip your Raven Beak's dagger from its sheath and stab at the barrier. It shatters in a brilliant explosion. The mage is free.
A crowd has gathered outside the home, a green glowing wall blocking all access. Destroying it will take more than a call to the Wyld.
<hero_name> thoughtfully observed the strange wall, realising a mere spell of the Wyld would not be enough to dissipate its presence.
The message came in urgent tones -- a loyal Bear Clan mage was trapped in his home by some magical barrier summoned by foul magic.
One of the Bear Clan's loyal mages is in mortal peril! His home is guarded by some magical barrier -- you've got to help him!
The Wall Betwixt
Break the chains apart. Surprise them!
Our hero struggled to break the chains, but it was to no avail. Through foul rituals, <hero_name> soon came to know the evils of the Rot.
You tug at the chains, but they are simply too strong to break. The cultists free you, but only after their rituals fill you with the Rot.
<hero_name> tore the chains apart, sending the cultists screaming in fear. Our hero freed their prisoners, ending the rituals for good.
Through the strength of the Bear Clan, the chains come undone. You free the other prisoners, gaining a valuable ally in the process!
Sneak away when the cultists are distracted.
<hero_name> waited and watched as countless innocents were dragged to their doom. Escape was easy, but the price was high. Too high.
You wait for the opportune moment as cultists drag countless innocents to their doom. You slip away unnoticed, but the cult remains.
"Hold still. Let me help!"
With some well timed sleight of hand, <hero_name>'s conjurer freed our hero. Together, they struck down their captors, and escaped.
The conjurer mutters. Magic crackles in the air. Your chains open. You attack! Wounding your captors then escaping to freedom.
"Psst! Over here!"
The faithful squire came to the aid of <hero_name> and hero and squire escaped the perilous depths and their malevolent captors!
Your faithful squire, having evaded your captors, sneaks over and unshackles you. Together you flee the depths, souvenir in tow!
"Releasing us will be worth it..."
With lies and empty promises, our hero's trader convinced the Rot Cultists to let them go. It would be weeks before the trick was discovered.
The Rot Cult's members lean in close as your trader begins to speak. Promising goods you know he doesn't have, he secures your release.
The moment you enter, the cultists ambush you! Held fast by a multitude of chains, they lead you deep into the bowels of the earth.
Unfortunately, the cultists knew <hero_name> was coming! They surprised our hero, binding with chains the only one capable of stopping them.
Our hero knew the quest was of dire importance: a Rot-worshipping cult could not be allowed to flourish in Armello! It had to be stopped.
Rumor has it that a Rot-worshipping cult has made a home for themselves in this old dungeon. Go and end their vile practices!
The Chains that Bind
Assist the mouse before thieves appear.
The treasure, alas, goes nowhere. <hero_name> tried to help, but simply lacked the strength! Rival treasure hunters soon claimed it instead!
Sadly, you are not strong enough to drag the treasure anywhere. Your path is quickly blocked by rival hunters, and you are forced to flee.
<hero_name> easily made off with the grand treasure, splitting it with the valiant mouse. The Bear Clan heirloom had been returned!
With your superior strength, you escape with the treasure. Even splitting it with the mouse, you reclaim a Bear Clan heirloom as a reward!
Turn against the mouse.
<hero_name> would never split Bear Clan heirlooms! Sadly, while our hero chased the mouse away, rival looters stole the grand treasure!
Why split Bear Clan treasures? You chase the mouse away, but return to find your loot stolen by a band of rival treasure hunters.
"Something heavy? I'm sure I can handle it!"
<hero_name>'s loyal smith lifted the treasure like he would a hammer at the forge. The three split the loot and went on their merry ways.
The Blacksmith lifts the massive treasure chest with ease, carrying it to safety. You split the treasures evenly between the three of you.
"Follow the beast!"
The Elk was not so magical as to not need sleep and water. With the spymaster's help, our hero tracked the beast to its riverside home.
The Elk runs. Lead by the spymaster, you follow. You find the creature asleep by a strange pond. Drinking from it strengthens you.
You arrive to find a small mouse desperately trying to drag a large treasure box from a broken-down caravan. He isn't making good progress.
<hero_name> found the treasure in the paws of a tiny mouse, though the diminutive creature seemed incapable of dragging the chest anywhere.
A great treasure of the Bear Clan had been stolen, but <hero_name> resolved to get it back! Would our hero reach it in time?
An old Bear Clan treasure went missin' a while back. Well, guess what? Rumor has it a bunch a' treasure hunters found it nearby.
Scavenger's Rights
Massacre the slavers.
Enraged at the thought of an entire town sold into tragic destinies, our hero picked a fight with all the slavers, quickly regretting it.
"Come out, slaver scum!" you scream. Unfortunately, it turns out the slavers are in far greater numbers than you thought. You flee, wounded.
In a display of martial prowess rarely seen, <hero_name> laid waste to each and every slaver. Liberating <quest_tile> was a bonus.
Thanks to your combat skills, the slavers are quick to fall. The grateful villagers hand you the slavers' most prized possession as thanks.
Challenge the slaver king.
In the streets, Slaver King and Bear Clan Hero met. In the end, it was just one swift blow from <hero_name> liberated <quest_tile>.
The slaver king proves all bluff, and you slay him before he can finish his threatening monologue. The slavers scatter in all directions.
Raise the Royal Banner
-Raising the Royal Banner, <hero_name> terrified the slavers into submission. They fled the settlement, leaving it safe once more.\n
You hold the Royal Banner high, displaying the Mad King's crest to the hidden slavers. Fearing your authority, they flee the settlement.
"The shadows will not hide them."
<hero_name>'s warlock unleashed the power of the Rot upon the hapless slavers. Their foul actions had been justly rewarded.
Your warlock twists the shadows hiding the slavers. Screams echo from within the closed houses. The village is safe again.
"Just say the word, I'm 'ere."
As the slavers descended upon our hero, it was the loyal Berserker who stood tall with <hero_name>, liberating <quest_tile> from evil.
Your Berserker snaps to your side, and the two of you extinguish every lowlife animal who enters your weapons' reach.
You wonder why nobody in town will speak with you, but it doesn't take long to notice slavers tracking you from behind shuttered windows.
After the few villagers left in <quest_tile> dodged questions, it was clear slavers had a tight choke hold on this community.
With rumours that <quest_tile> is now a ghost town, our hero set off on what seemed to be a mass missing persons case.
A once bustling trade town's inhabitants are now few. Find out what happened to this settlement's population.
The Ghost Town
Slay the Banes in open combat.
In a bid our to vanquish them before they're too powerful, our hero charged the Banes, but alas they proved too many, wounding <hero_name>.
Unfortunately, you lack the skill to defeat the Banes and flee in failure. The Rot continues to fester in that village to this very day.
Knowing that death begets death, <hero_name> charged the Banes, slaying them all. The relieved settlers offered a Spirit Stone in thanks.
You charge the Banes, relying on your vast combat skill to protect you. The town is soon purged, and you receive a Spirit Stone as a reward.
Employ the remaining townsfolk to help.
And so, <hero_name> rallied the remaining townsfolk. Though many lives were lost in the ensuing battle, <quest_tile> was safe again.
You beg the townsfolk to help you destroy their corrupted kin. Many lives are lost in the ensuing battle, but the Banes are soon destroyed.
Load the Hand Cannons
The Banes were not ready for the fury of the Hand Cannons. They were slain, or fled, leaving the village forever.
The Hand Cannons flash! Fire and smoke taint the air. The Banes shriek. Those that don't flee are slain.
Raise your shield
Our hero just had time to raise their Royal Shield before the Banes fell upon them. <hero_name> was not overcome! They fought back, and won!
The rattling strikes of a dozen Bane's Blades clang against your Royal Shield. None pierce! You slay the Banes, freeing the village.
"Let's put on a little show!"
From a vial of lively green, a wyldfyre phoenix emerged, vanquishing the beasts. In the fire's light, the Alchemist's wry grin glistened.
The Alchemist throws a vial to the ground and with fiery fury a green phoenix erupts, vanquishing the Banes one by one.
Directed by the settlers, you quickly find yourself surrounded by Banes of all sizes. You must act quickly to stop this evil from spreading!
It was soon apparent our hero was too late. Banes of all sizes moved through the town, the terror of their wrath too heinous for words.
Hearing rumours of sacrifice and dark pacts, <hero_name> made haste for <quest_tile> to end the needless slaughter.
Settlers within the woods are sacrificing their kin to Banes in a bid for leniency. Intervene before these fools waste more lives.
The Forest Purge
Attempt to approach the elk.
But it was the elk's eyes that proved too much for our hero, <hero_name>'s mind wilting in its intense gaze.
The elk turns to face you, its gaze is so intense that you feel your mind cracking. As you break eye contact you feel wiser, yet weakened.
With simply a gaze, hero and elk spoke. A Spirit Stone revealing itself just as <hero_name>'s path became clearer than ever before.
You approach the elk. It turns to face you and while no words are exchanged, this ancient being infuses you with an unwavering motivation.
Leave the elk be.
From afar, our hero gazed upon the majestic creature as it grazed the plains and deep down, <hero_name> knew they'd never forget this.
You keep your distance. Briefly the elk gazes at you from afar, and you realize this is truly a god before you. It nods, then disappears.
"I want to play!"
The strange ways of <quest_tile>'s fool amused the elk. It gifted unto him ancient secrets, which he shared with our hero.
Before you can object, your fool leaps at the Elk. To your shock, it doesn't flee. Instead, it whispers to him, secrets he passes on to you.
Watch the Elk.
<hero_name> lay in wait, hidden by the Mirror Cape. Watching the Elk reinforced our hero's connection with the Wyld.
Hidden by the cape's skillful craftsmanship, you lie low in the grass. As you watch, you feel as if some of the creature's magic strengthens you.
As you stand in the long grass, you spy something ahead; a great elk. A coat of almond gold, antlers of ivory and eyes of diamond blue.
After a long journey, our hero arrived at <quest_tile>. Before too long, the majestic elk showed itself. A god before our hero's very eyes.
Surely a god above all else could assist our hero on their quest for the throne. And so <hero_name>'s pilgrimage for the Great Elk began...
