<hero_name> charged, but the Rabbit Clan was ready! It was a desperate battle, but our hero was forced to flee with a wound most terrible.
You charge the Rabbit Clan warriors, but they were suspecting trouble from the Rat Clan today! You are nearly cut down, and forced to flee.
<hero_name> yelled and charged into the crowd, cutting a path of fury through the square. All prisoners escaped, thanks to our hero's deeds!
You charge the Rabbit Clan warriors and begin slaying them left and right. Escape is quick, and all your friends make it out alive!
Free the other prisoners.
<hero_name> crept through the crowd to the prisoners' cells. The executioner's axe took many lives that day, but our hero saved many more!
You sneak past the chopping block and quietly free the other prisoners. The THUNK of the axe reminds you that you could not save them all.
Cause a panic
A journey's worth of syphoning magic into the Bane's Claw was put to use. Our hero used it to cause a panic, letting them free the rats.
Out of options, you raise the Bane's Claw. You release the magic within, letting Rot pour through the air. The crowd scatters, letting you free the rats.
"Save the Rats!"
Rats know trickery well. But our hero also knew the ways of raw strength, thanks to their berserker. They charged. The rats were freed.
Your Berserker has come up with the most elegant solution. He charges the platform, battering the executioners and freeing the captive rats.
Push your Loyal squire into the crowd. Distract them!
"Think fast!" Our hero shoved their loyal squire into the crowd, distracting the guards and allowing them to free all the prisoners safely!
You push your squire into the crowd, causing a commotion that distracts the guards long enough for you to free the prisoners.
You hurry into town to find a staunch Rat Clan supporter being pushed down onto the chopping block. You must act quickly!
<hero_name> made haste to the village, knowing every lost minute could be a lost life. Our hero arrived just as the executioner's axe rose.
The Rabbit Clan had gone a step too far, capturing Rat Clan loyalists and planning to execute them in a nearby village.
There are Rat Clan loyalists slated to be executed in <quest_tile> by some Rabbit Clan sympathizers. Best go save 'em!
Off With Their Heads!
Enter the old ruin!
Unfortunately, <hero_name> was anything BUT strong with the Wyld, and realized rather quickly that attempting to pass only meant death.
You reach a paw out and feel... cold. A terrible darkness tugs at your very soul, and you realize you will never pass this barrier alive.
Fortunately, <hero_name> was indeed strong with the Wyld, and passed through with haste to claim the Spirit Stone for the Rat Clan.
You reach a paw out and feel a comforting warmth around you. The curtain lifts, and the ruin (and its Spirit Stone) are opened to you.
Explore the outside.
So, instead of risking life and limb with the magic barrier, our hero took the time to explore the ruins, to get closer to the Wyld.
You decide to stay outside -- that barrier could very well mean your death. You feel stronger with the Wyld after a stroll, at least.
"We will walk on..."
The ways of the Wyld and magic are commonplace to the stranger. He lead our hero into the ancient ruin. It's cold magic leaking into them.
The stranger puts your paw on his shoulder and leads you through the barricade. You split the treasures you find within.
Cut through the haze
The mist would not part, but the Wyld recognised <hero_name> as a hero. It blessed them with magic, channelled through the Moon Scythe.
As you draw the moon scythe, the trials of your quest flash into mind. The scythe glows. Mist wraps around it. Magic flows through you.
The Wyld Talisman shimmers.
The Wyld seemed to communicate with <hero_name>'s Wyld Talisman, a mote of the haze's power drifted into the amulet.
You lift the Wyld Talisman high and feel a harsh wave of Wyld flow into it. The haze remains, but the magic you've stolen will be useful.
The old ruin seems guarded by the Wyld itself -- a haze draped about it like a curtain over the very fabric of reality.
Alas, the barrier seemed to be comprised of the Wyld itself, and only one strong in its ways could pass through it unhindered.
An old Bear Clan ruin held a Spirit Stone behind a strange magical barrier -- perhaps our hero could find a way through it?
Found an old ruin from the days when the Bear Clan had such things. Seems there's a Spirit Stone there if yer interested?
Enclave of the Wyld
Help! You must!
<hero_name> begged the Wyld to come to the creature's aid, but no help came. The creature soon turned, striking Rot into our hero's soul.
You reach out a paw, but the Wyld does not heed your call. The patient hisses a vile curse at you, and you feel a cold grip on your soul.
But <hero_name> wouldn't let the Rot take them! Begging the Wyld for aid, the loyalist was purged of their affliction to fight another day!
You reach out a paw and feel the Wyld surge through you. The healer is astonished to see her patient rise up, cured, and join your cause!
Put the loyalist out of their misery.
Alas, there was never any guarantee of the Wyld's help. <hero_name> drove a dagger into the loyalist's chest, ending their suffering.
Best avoid the Rot taking them, you think. You drive your blade into the loyalist's heart, and apologize to the healer for the trouble.
Transfer the sickness to the Poppet
The poppet, often a tool of darkness, could also be used to heal. <hero_name> transferred the sickness off the loyalist. Saving him.
You lay the doll down by the loyalist and begin a chant. Slowly, the Rot creeps across to the doll. The loyalist is left weak, but alive.
"The Rot here has power"
There was no hope for the loyalist, but they could still serve the Rat clan in death. <hero_name>'s warlock used the Rot to create a powerful spell.
Your warlock leans over the loyalist's quivering body. "He can't be saved..." You nod. The warlock raises his paw. The room grows cold.
"This one is done for, but I can still salvage something."
<hero_name>'s alchemist was quick to turn the loyalist's inevitable demise to your gain, draining their blood to create a powerful spell!
Your Alchemist draws blood from the dying creature and distills it into a valuable spell -- though the Rat Clan loyalist quickly perishes.
You enter a healer's hut and notice the patient on a small bed, eyes turning purple with Rot. "Just a matter of time now," the healer sighs.
The situation was grim, to be sure. The creature's eyes were turning a cloudy purple, their mind slowly descending into darkness.
A loyal friend to the Rat Clan was dying -- afflicted by the Rot with not much time remaining. Our hero went to see what could be done.
Probably not worth mentionin', but a Rat Clan loyalist is in a nearby settlement dyin' from Rot. Not much can be done now, though...
Just a Matter of Time
Beg the Wyld to spare your friend and put him to rest.
<hero_name> begged the Wyld to intervene, but no help came. Benvolo's cursed form attacked our hero then, and the Rot took hold.
You beg the Wyld for aid that never comes. Your friend's rotting form slashes at you -- a living darkness seeping deep under your fur.
<hero_name> couldn't stand to see an old friend suffer so, and begged the Wyld for aid. A blinding light freed Benvolo, and all was right.
The decrepit form of Benvolo staggers toward you, but a blinding light fills the plains with a healing warmth. His bones collapse, inert.
Slash your friends bones until they fall.
<hero_name> slashed and hacked at Benvolo's cursed form until it fell, then buried his bones until the shrieks could no longer be heard.
You slash at your friend's cursed form until it cannot support its own weight. You bury the bones while his skull continues to snap at you.
"Cursed friend, yeah? I know a spell for that one."
<hero_name>'s apprentice had a solution: a spell that lifted Benvolo's spirit and left his cursed bones to fall to the earth.
The apprentice leaps forward, magic flowing from his paws. Your friend's spirit is lifted, and his cursed bones fall lifelessly to the dirt.
Force him back with the Royal Shield
Benvolo's bones would not cease their attack. <hero_name> weathered his blows, but saw no way out. Our hero struck, shattering the skeleton.
Benvolo's strikes rain down about the shield, but it holds! Finally, with a mighty strike, you shatter his bones. He is at peace. At last.
"Yoink! More Bones! Yoink!"
Benvolo's fate would have made him laugh. The fool snatched away his bones one by one, until at last the skeleton collapsed. Unable to move.
As you stare aghast, the fool begins to snatch away crucial limbs. Bit by bit the skeleton falls apart. The fool grins. "Yoink!"
The journey to your old friend's grave is a sad one -- sadder still when you realize his restless bones have been given form by the Rot!
But the poor rat had perished on the road in the plains -- worse yet, his bones had been consumed by Rot, possessing them to foul ends.
Benvolo of Midvale was one of the finest thieves in the Rat Clan -- a dear friend of our hero, who fought alongside them many times.
You remember Benvolo, the chief thief of Midvale? Perished, sadly. His bones were found on the road, deep in the plains.
Last Respects
Rely on your wits to bypass the traps.
It would be one of these traps, a poison dart, that nearly took <hero_name>'s life and forced a hasty retreat from the warren!
You accidentally set off one of the traps, taking a rather painful poison dart to the neck. You flee the old warren, sensing death ahead.
But even the Rabbit Clan's best was no match for our hero's wits! The traps were quickly disarmed, and the treasure lay unguarded!
You easily sense and disarm all traps guarding the vault at the other end of the passage. Inside, a Spirit Stone glows with pure light.
Avoid the trap-laden passage.
The traps proved too daunting for our hero, but the wealth of archaic knowledge in the warren turned out to be a useful consolation prize!
Ignoring the trap-laden passage, you find many intriguing parchments lost to time that help you bolster your knowledge of Armello.
Don the Lionheart Breastplate
Our hero strapped on their Lionheart Breastplate and walked down the deadly corridor without a fear. They looted the warren with ease.
The traps fire a deadly hail of bolts down at you, but each bounces off your breastplate. You stroll along the passage, grinning. Easy!
Push the squire forward
The squire was.... encouraged to test the traps for our hero. <hero_name> split the treasure with them, as reward for their bravery.
Yelping in pain, the squire rushes along the hall, battered by deadly traps. You stroll after him. The two of you split the treasure.
The warren's tunnel ends at a stone door with blue light bleeding from the edges. You do not see it, but you know the passage is trapped.
The place was long-abandoned, but the mark of the Rabbit Clan's inventors remained. There was no doubt a trap or two laying just ahead.
Not all treasures glow blue -- only Spirit Stones. It was this simple fact that drew <hero_name> to the stories of the old warren.
Rumor has it there's an ancient Rabbit Clan warren here in Armello. Past the deadly traps and pitfalls, a sacred treasure awaits!
The Old Warren
Work through the poison, slay the barkeep.
Unfortunately, our hero wasn't strong enough to fight the poison and was soundly robbed, then unceremoniously dumped in a nearby alley.
You try to fight the poison, but when you stand you lose all strength and collapse to the floor. You awaken much later, robbed of your gold.
But our hero was stronger than the poison, fighting through it and slaying the barkeep with a tremendous leap over the bar!
Fighting the poison, you leap the counter and slam your dagger into the barkeep's chest. It's not a total loss: he had a follower's card!
Flee the pub and hide amongst the crowd.
Knowing the poison would quickly incapacitate, our hero stumbled away into the thick crowds of the village, disappearing from sight.
Before he can react, you stumble away from the devious barkeep and disappear into the crowd. You awaken in a trash-strewn alley hours later.
"Smells like nightshade poison. Here, drink this."
Fortunately, <hero_name>'s Apothecary was quick with the antidote, allowing our hero to chase down the devious barkeep in short order!
Your Apothecary hands you the antidote, and the poison's advance is halted. The barkeep flees -- but you and your dagger soon catch him.
"Out! Quick!"
Thankfully, <hero_name>'s conjurer spotted the treachery early. He picked the bartender's pocket, stealing an antidote, and a spell card.
Your conjurer drags you outside. You can hardly breathe. He shoves a bottle into your hands. "He had the antidote in his pocket. Drink!"
The village is quite nice -- why, the barkeep even offers you a free pint! Only it tastes... off. Could it-? Yes, it's definitely poisoned.
Everything seemed quite normal, really. Kind people, kind barkeep -- the free pint was nice, too! Until <hero_name> tasted the poison.
Rumors had been circulating of a nearby town that wasn't very welcoming to the Rat Clan. Our hero set about to uncover the truth.
I'd be careful about visitin' that town nearby. Word is they've got it out for the Rat Clan!
A Stale Pint
Scale the tower, steal the card back.
Our hero boldly began to climb, but it was clear the top was out of reach. <hero_name> fell, striking the earth with a most painful crunch.
You begin to climb, but it's clear you're not strong enough to make it. Your grip weakens and you fall to the earth with a painful crunch.
Yet the tower proved no issue for our brave hero, and the follower's card was quickly back in the Rat Clan's claws.
You skitter up the tower with ease, your claws finding even the smallest handholds. You take the mark and leave a dagger in its place.
Break in through the front door.
Our hero tried sneaking in through the front door, but the guards were quick to react. Still, <hero_name> was stronger for the effort!
You pick the lock on the door and begin to sneak up the long way. Unfortunately, the tower's guards spot you long before you reach the top.
"A little magic will go a long way here. Can I help?"
Our hero was made invisible by their apprentice, allowing easy entry to the tower. The card was gone, but a valuable item took its place!
The apprentice whispers a simple spell and you are made invisible. You don't find the card, but do make off with the knight's valuables!
"Here, try these."
Our hero was able to scale the walls with special boots built by the blacksmith. The mark was gone, but another treasure was found.
The Blacksmith hands over a pair of special climbing boots.  You don't find the mark, but you rob the castle vault!
The knight's tower on the plains was poorly-defended, at least on the outside. An open window near the top would grant easy entry...
<hero_name> would not stand idly by! The knight lived in a tall tower, and the follower's card would be locked away somewhere inside.
It is suicide to rob the Rat Clan, yet they always try. In this case, a rogue knight had spirited away a follower's card meant for our hero.
A rogue knight robbed one of our brothers and made off with a follower's card meant for you. No worries, though -- I know where he lives.
The Tall Tower
Help the slaves through the toughest part of the swamp.
Unfortunately, the dangers of the swamp proved too much for our hero, and many slaves lost their lives in the mire that fateful day.
You try to help the slaves escape the vile marsh, but you are simply not strong enough. Many slaves perish during your daring escape.
Fortunately, our hero was strong of body and mind, leading the freed slaves to safety through the deadly mire and away from the slavers!
Using your strength, you are able to help even the most vulnerable slaves escape the swamp. They have little, but reward you all the same.
Tell the slaves to scatter. Best way to confuse the slavers!
To confuse the slavers, <hero_name> ordered the prisoners to scatter. Unfortunately, many slaves perished in those vile swamps as a result.
You tell the slaves to split up, knowing deep down most will not escape the swamp alive. Still, the few who do escape are grateful to you.
"There is a little-known path that will lead us to safety!"
It was only through the actions of <hero_name>'s loyal Explorer that a secret path was found for the slaves to escape unhindered.
Your loyal Explorer knows these swamps well, and leads you and the escaped slaves down ancient, hidden pathways to freedom.
"Home."
It would seem the Stranger is not a complete mystery. He deigned to show our hero his home, in an attempt to help the freed slaves.
Revealing something about himself for the first time, The Stranger takes you to a nearby hut. There, the slaves find food and shelter.
Forge a path with the Wyldfyre Staff
The Wyldfyre Staff channeled magic at our hero's request, clearing a path through the treacherous marsh for <hero_name> and the slaves.
The staff's magic, sensing the purity of your journey, clears a path through the swamp. The slaves hurry on, cheering. They will be safe.
You come across the slave caravan as it carefully navigates a lightning-sand bog. With a quick slice of your dagger, the slaves are free!
Finding the caravan was easy, as was freeing the slaves from the inattentive slavers. The problem was escaping the deadly swamp alive.
A local slaver was plying his trade in a nearby swamp, angering our hero to action. <hero_name> resolved to end the foul practice!
Word is there's a slave caravan bringin' Rat Clan prisoners through these swamps. Best find 'em and end this foul practice!
A Dash in the Swamp
Track the blood and find the spy.
Our hero searched for hours, but the missing spy remained elusive. A handful of the his burnt reports would be this journey's only prize.
You search and search, but the spy remains as elusive as you'd expect. A few burnt parchments of useless intelligence is all you find.
The spy -- and his attacker -- were easily found nearby, the two having slain each another at once. Their secrets now belonged to our hero.
You find the body of the informant, and his Wolf Clan killer. You claim a useful follower's card from their belongings, the mystery solved.
Leave the spy for dead and claim his reports.
The spy was lost, but not his wealth of ill-gained intelligence! Our hero claimed what remained before leaving the mountaintop.
Knowing that whatever fate befell the spy probably occurred days ago, you claim whatever intelligence you can find before leaving.
Place the poppet in the blood
The informant had vanished, even to this day, his fate is unknown. Luckily, his blood was put to use through the Poppet's magic.
The doll hums as you lay it in the dried blood. You feel magic flow through you. The informant is gone, but his blood will be useful.
Use the Winged Boots to get a bird's eye view.
It was only by donning the enchanted Winged Boots that our hero found the spy's body, and the vital intelligence he had died protecting.
The boots allow you a bird's eye view, revealing the spy's resting place. You claim his lost secrets before moving on.
"Blood? Perfect."
The informant had vanished. To this day, none know of his fate. Luckily, our hero's alchemist was able to harness the dried blood for magic.
The Alchemist hurries forward. Although the informant is gone, his lifeblood can be distilled into a powerful spell.
You ascend the peak to find naught but an abandoned campfire and a few old bloodstains that hint at some greater malice. Betrayal?
Alas, the spy was nowhere to be seen. A toppled table set for two offered a possible hint to the rogue's fate.
A Rat Clan informant was holding court on <quest_tile>. It was time to learn what secrets they held.
Word is there's an informant loyal to the Rat Clan waiting for you on a nearby mountain peak. Might be worthwhile to see what they know.
One of Us
Convince the captain to give you his sole support.
Unfortunately, the captain was quick to dismiss <hero_name>, leaving the pub with more than a few harsh words for the Rat Clan.
You try to lay on the charm, but the turncoat captain is not swayed. He declares the Rat Clan not worth his time and hastily exits the pub.
Yet through a combination of charm and menace, our hero managed to convince the traitorous captain to turn to the Rat Clan once and for all.
You expertly convince the captain that his best interests lie solely with you. He offers a trinket as a sign of loyalty before leaving.
Threaten the captain into serving the Rat Clan.
<hero_name>'s dagger made the argument, and the captain was quick to concede. He pledged support to the Rat Clan, fearful for his life.
A dagger to the throat has a way of forcing the mind into action, as demonstrated by the traitorous captain's hasty pledge to the Rat Clan.
"See this pardon? I could slay you without consequence."
The threat of murder without consequence was more than enough to shake the captain into pledging his allegiance to the Rat Clan.
The captain's eyes dance across the parchment. He stands and pledges fealty to the Rat Clan, offering a sign of goodwill before he leaves.
Show the Royal Banner
By showing the Royal Banner, our hero reminded the treacherous captain of his duties. He swore fealty to <hero_name> once more.
"When you fund my enemies. You fund the king's enemies!" The captain looks down. Ashamed. His colleagues shift away from him.
Turn the captains troops against him
There were still righteous folk within the Kingdom of Armello. <hero_name> revealed the captains treachery, and his colleagues took him prisoner.
As the captain stands, ready to attack, you slip on the Masquerade Mask. With a rousing speech, you reveal his corruption. His troops arrest him.
You enter the pub and sit across the table from the treacherous captain, slamming a dagger into the splintered wood. Time to make your move.
Our hero confronted him in a seedy pub, the telltale glints of daggers and swords in the dim light giving the meeting an air of malice.
A high-ranking captain loyal to the crown was sending gold to <hero_name>'s enemies. Clearly this could not stand.
Rumor has it a high-ranking captain in the King's Guard is funding your enemies. Confront him and put an end to his treachery.
The Traitorous Captain
Ask the Wyld to free these beasts of Rot.
Alas, the Wyld is a fickle thing, and our hero was unable to summon its light. The groundskeeper was lost, and our hero was forced to flee.
The Wyld does not answer. You can do nothing but watch as the groundskeeper is devoured. Knowing you will be next, you flee the swamp.
Fortunately, our hero was well-attuned to the Wyld, able to cleanse the beasts of their Rot and save the groundskeeper from a terrible fate.
A blinding light fills the swamp, killing the spiders. The groundskeeper is grateful for your help, offering a Spirit Stone as reward.
Draw the spiders' attention away.
Thinking quickly, our hero relied on a well-placed dagger to draw the spiders away from the groundskeeper, giving her time to escape.
You throw a dagger at the nearest spider, drawing their gaze and leading them away. The groundskeeper escapes, but you know not where to.
"These creatures are filled with Rot. Allow me."
It was thanks to the Warlock's mastery of the Rot that the spiders were driven away without conflict. The groundskeeper escaped unharmed.
The spiders screech and hiss, the Rot shifting across their jet black forms. They scuttle away, allowing the groundskeeper to escape.
Open Fire!
The Hand Cannons proved strong enough to force back the spiders. The groundskeeper, grateful, gave our hero a gift.
The hand cannons flash in your paws. The spiders chitter, fleeing into the trees. The groundskeeper is safe. Thanks to you quick aim.
Force the Rot Beasts back!
The spiders were overcome by the cleansing power of the Wyld. Our hero cut them down with the Moon Scythe. Freeing the groundskeeper.
The Moon Scythe glows brilliant white as you raise it. The spiders shriek, blinded. You cut them down, letting the groundskeeper escape.
The king's personal groundskeeper is easy to spot -- she stands in the center of a trio of massive, hungry, Rot-infested spiders!
Upon arriving, the groundskeeper's plight was clear: a trio of Rot-infested spiders surrounded her. She was moments from death!
The royal groundskeeper had gone missing, but rumor had it she was lost in a nearby swamp. Our hero made haste for the mire.
I've gotten word that the king's groundskeeper is lost in <quest_tile>! If you save her, I'm sure she'd offer a nice reward!
Lost in the Mire
Summon the Wyld to deal with the boars.
The Wyld would not respond to our hero's call that day. As <hero_name> watched helplessly, the wagon continued along the plain.
You whisper to the Wyld, but it does not heed your call. You stand helplessly as the wagon rolls on unimpeded across the plain.
The Wyld would deal with these brutes without issue. A gust of wind rolled the wagon right over them, freeing the prisoner at the same time.
A terrible gust of wind issues forth, and the wagon flips over, crushing the guards. The prisoner is freed, and pledges support to you.
Ask the Wyld to shroud the plains in fog.
The Wyld helped our hero save the prisoner, though the guards were not pleased. The battle was brief, but the Rat Clan emerged victorious.
A fog appears, but it is not enough to mask your movements. The prisoner is wounded in the escape -- enough to keep them from joining you.
"Follow my lead"
Rather than attack the boars head on, our hero chose a stealthier approach at the Spymaster's request. The prisoner was saved. A close call.
Your spymaster leads you over to the wagon, hidden. You slice open the back, free the prisoner, and take a little something extra as well.
Hold your Bane's Blade aloft
The guards fled in terror from the cursed blade, giving our hero ample time to free the prisoner and claim a reward for their help.
The guards see your blade from a distance and are quick to flee. The prisoner is grateful, but wary of joining one wielding such a blade.
Armour yourself and attack!
Our hero fought to free the prisoner. Grateful, they gave our hero a gift, before fleeing into Armello's mountains.
No Boar has the strength to strike though the Helm of Heroes. You hold them off long enough for the prisoner to escape. Then retreat.
The locked prison wagon rolls lazily along the path, pulled by a pair of brutish boars. You mustn't let the wagon travel too far.
The prison wagon rolled lazily along the path, guarded by a pair of boars. <hero_name> watched from afar, planning the daring escape.
Framed for a murder they did not commit, a loyal Rat Clan follower was en route to the gallows. Time was not on <hero_name>'s side.
A supporter of the Rat Clan rots in a prison wagon. If you were to free them, I'm sure they would prove to be a loyal follower.
Chains of Custody
Summon the Wyld to produce a dire omen.
The Wyld could have helped, but it chose to ignore our hero's pleas. The meeting concluded, and our hero was forced to flee in failure.
The Wyld ignores your call, leaving you to watch as the two clans come together in an alliance that will only serve to disrupt the Rat Clan.
It was the Wyld that solved the problem: the sky turned a terrifying blood red, hinting at ill, dire omens. The alliance was over.
The Wyld turns the sky blood red. The rabbit and bear are horrified by this, realizing that perhaps the Wyld does not favor their alliance.
Disrupt the meeting and delay the alliance.
Our hero stormed into the stone circle, forcing the clans to adjourn. An alliance between the two clans was, sadly, still inevitable.
You walk into the circle, surprising both the bear and the rabbit. The meeting is adjourned, but your know it only delays the inevitable.
"I have proof these clans are unfit for alliance. Allow me."
It was only thanks to the Coin Master's exhaustively-collected proof of foul play between the two clans that their alliance is broken apart.
The Coin Master disrupts the meeting with claims of paid assassinations, incriminating both clans against one another. The two part ways.
Sneak close and listen
Shadows and deceit are the domain of rats! Our hero crept close and listened in. Their schemes would be useless now.
The glimmering Mirror Cape lets you draw up close to the meet. The secrets you hear will be useful in the coming days.
"Really? Even after the Fleetfoot purge?"
The bear and rabbit clans have been enemies since as long as any can remember. All they needed was a reminder, and the Bard provided one.
Your bard steps forth, tales of bear atrocities committed on rabbits tumbling from his lips. After this reminder, the talks collapse.
You notice the local leaders of both the Bear and Rabbit Clans conversing in hushed, but friendly tones. This will not do at all.
Our hero crept around the stone circle. The bear and rabbit were there, speaking in friendly tones -- a tone of allies. This needed to stop.
Rumors reached our hero of an alliance brewing between the Bear and Rabbit Clans. If true, it could have spelled disaster for the Rat Clan.
I've heard the Rabbit and Bear Clans are planning a secret meeting nearby. Maybe an alliance? You should see what they're up to.
Clan Collusion
Sneak through the castle and slay the wolves.
While the plan was sound, our hero's fighting skills were not. The Wolf Clan easily gained the upper hand, forcing <hero_name> to flee.
Unfortunately, the wolves quickly spot you, converging on you with the fury renowned of their clan. You flee the castle in failure.
That plan involved steel -- and lots of it. <hero_name> crept through the old castle, slaying each and every wolf until none remained.
Not a single wolf survives your onslaught, which comes as silently and swiftly as the night itself. The castle and its treasures are yours.
Offer a compromise to the Wolf Clan.
Relying on the appearance of strength, our hero gave the wolves an ultimatum: share the profits, or die. The wolves, thankfully, accepted.
When you're certain the wolves can see you, you offer amnesty in exchange for half the castle's earnings. Amused, they accept the agreement.
Storm the castle with the Royal Shield as your defence.
Under any other circumstance, storming the castle would have been most unwise. But the Royal Shield guarded our hero from all harm.
The wolves' blows bounce harmlessly off your shield, and you manage to cleanse the castle of their presence without so much as a scratch.
"They're clueless."
Running a gambling den is much more complicated than the wolves knew. They were forced to ask for help, help which the Trader would charge for.
Trader by your side, you approach. The wolves have no idea how to run a den. They offer you a cut to run the place, and you rob them blind.
"We can always collapse the castle."
The Gambling den had stood for many years, but could not stand forever. With the miner's help, our hero collapsed it. Killing all inside.
Better the gambling den be destroyed than fall to Wolves. With the Miner's help, you weaken key supports. It collapses, killing all inside.
You stand before the remains of an old castle, home of the Rat Clan's hidden gambling empire -- though now the Wolf Clan has taken charge.
The question was, how? The Wolf Clan was guarding the old castle and its grounds day and night. <hero_name> needed a plan.
The forest gambling den was a Rat Clan institution... until the Wolf Clan took it over. Our hero resolved to reclaim it.
Rumor has it an ancient Rat Clan gambling den deep in the forest has been taken over by the Wolf Clan. Your superiors will want it back.
The Gambling Den
Prove the Rat Clan deserves the throne. Slay them all.
Beset upon by the assassins, our hero stood little chance of success. Thankfully, the tall grass proved a useful shroud in escaping death.
Without the element of surprise, you are quickly wounded. You lose them in the tall grass, but only after throwing some gold to divert them.
The bear and wolf quickly fell to our hero's flashing blade, but the rabbit escaped -- trading the favour of a local hero for her life.
Your dagger flies, ending the bear's life first. The wolf perishes next, but the rabbit offers a follower's card in exchange for her life.
Escape the assassins in the tall grass.
Knowing a losing battle when it presented itself, our hero vanished into the tall grass, eluding the assassins and escaping the trap.
With nothing but a grin, you duck into the tall grass, vanishing from sight completely. You are lucky to escape with your life!
"These fools stand no chance."
The Berserker, however, was not interested in escaping the ambush. His axe felled the three assassins with ease, saving our hero's life.
The Berserker marches forward, his axe immediately taking down the horrified bear. The wolf and rabbit try to flee, but do not get far.
Show them true power
Our hero's Raven's Beak Dagger bolstered their strength. <hero_name> slew the assassins, proving the rat clan masters of cloak and dagger.
No beast is better assassin than a rat. You beckon them over, then strike with the Raven's Beak dagger. They fall. You harness their power.
Call the Wyld to protect you
The assassins were foiled by our hero's Wyld Talisman. Using it's power, <hero_name> was able to escape.
The Wyld will not let such injustice go ahead. It responds as you raise the talisman, calling a thick mist which lets you escape.
You sense that you are not alone as you walk the plains, and quickly find yourself surrounded by wolf, rabbit, and bear assassins!
The bear was the first to make his presence known, and the wolf and rabbit hid nearby. Our hero needed to act quickly to escape the ambush!
The other clans were getting desperate -- their finest assassins had joined forces to slay our hero on the open plains.
Stories abound of an alliance of assassins from the Rabbit, Bear, and Wolf Clans working to end your life somewhere in these plains.
Ambush on the Plains
Draw your blade and confront the demon.
It was a Bane! Our hero fought valiantly, but the embodiment of the Rot was far too powerful to destroy, forcing them to flee the keep.
You discover it is a Bane that hunts you in the darkness! It thrashes you with blows of pure Rot, forcing you to retreat in terror.
It was a Bane! Our hero relied on brute strength to bring it down, not only slaying it, but gaining the allegiance of a fellow adventurer.
With tremendous skill, the vile Bane soon falls to your blade. You search its victims and find a follower's card amongst their belongings.
Loot the nearest chest and flee.
Our hero knew a confrontation with ancient evil was best avoided if possible. After looting a nearby chest, they escaped the keep unharmed.
No point in sticking around if you don't have to! You open the closest treasure chest and grab the shiniest object within before fleeing.
Hold the Bane's Claw aloft. End the fight before it starts.
Fortunately, our hero held the storied Bane's Claw, forcing the eldritch horror of the lost keep back into the darkness once and for all.
You hold up the claw and stand your ground. When the vile Bane rounds the corner, it hisses and shrieks, disappearing in a black cloud.
"AHHHHHH!"
The fool had been through much on the journey, and seeing a monster in the deep proved the final straw. He cried so loud, the beast fled.
Your fool screams. Luckily for you, the sound is enough to make the creature cautious. You have time to loot the nearest chest and escape.
The twisting corridors whistle haunting hymns as you move through this ungodly place. A dark menace stirs somewhere in the darkness ahead...
Deep within the keep, our hero found a dank maze of twisting passages and locked doors... and something else. A sinister evil awakened!
An ancient Rat Clan keep lay deep underground, lost for generations. <hero_name> would be the first to open its doors in centuries.
There are long-standing rumours of a forgotten keep in Armello that was home to a mad tinkerer. Find it and see what treasures lie within.
The Bane of the Deep
Enter the palace walls.
<hero_name> slipped through a secret passage and into the palace grounds. The throne, and its mad occupant, were finally within reach.
You enter the palace without a sound, the path to the King before you. The path to your journey's end. The path to the throne of Armello.
The palace spires pierce the sky high above. Barely hidden by meticulously-crafted topiary, is your entrance: a metal grate, slightly ajar.
The palace walls had defended Armello's king from armies, spies, and assassins -- but it would not stop the Rat Clan.
The Rat Clan's agents had found our hero a safe path through the palace's many perils -- a path straight to the king's very throne room!
Rat agents have found a weakness in the king's defences -- it is time for the Rat Clan to take the throne!
The Final Battle
Whistle a Rat Clan tune.
<hero_name> whistled an ancient Rat Clan song, drawing in the Spy Master from her hiding place in the shadows. Their quest could begin.
You pick an obscure song. One you'd only know if you were listening for it. It takes just a few notes before the Spymaster sits next to you.
The city is bustling. You enter the tavern and glance around. There are many faces but none you've seen before. No Spymaster.
After claiming the bounty, our hero entered Southbank. They knew not where to start their search for the spy, so they visited the tavern.
<hero_name> journeyed towards the palace. They had two goals. To claim the bounty on Thane's head, and track down the Spymaster.
You have your orders. The Spymaster is waiting for you at Southbank.
Rat Clan Jingle
Sneak past him.
Nobody can spot a rat. Our hero crept past the foolish guard. Whatever Thane's plans were, Mercurio would know soon.
You're a shadow in the moonlight. He doesn't see you sneak by, close enough to touch. The contact, a miner, smiles and lets you in.
Signal to the contact
Our hero could not meet the contact personally, but they managed to get the information anyway, using a kind of dead drop.
A small spark lets the contact know you're there. She signals back, then tosses down a letter. A dead drop. You have the information.
The city curfew is in effect at nightfall. The contact's house is across the street, but a King's guard is patrolling in front of it.
Although our hero arrived at the settlement without issue, a curfew was in effect. A King's Guard patrolled the street.
Our hero's spymaster had tracked down the Rot relic to the Winterhorn Mountains. Our hero started towards them.
The Spymaster has tracked the stolen Rot tool to the Winterhorn Mountains. One of her sources in the city knows those peaks well.
Chasing Shadows
