Palace Entry
Rewards
Take over. You will feed on this power.
The deep halls' peril was clear. Our hero's darkness drifted in, but was forced back by fire and steel. Soon. Soon they would return.
The attendants are no challenge, they fall to your blade. But the head torturer forces you back with red hot steel. You flee, injured.
Deep within the dark, our hero fed on the power of pain long past. As their Rot grew, they took the time to inflict some pain of their own.
Those who don't flee are cut down before you. You strap the head torturer to the rack. Let him feel the irony as his bones are rent apart.
Kill the prisoners
Fire and steel held our hero back from the attendants, but could not save the prisoners. Without them, the King's strength would lessen.
The torturers can defend themselves, but not slow you down. You slay the prisoners. Let the King find his power elsewhere.
Display the Poppet
The Poppet has been a tool of pain since its creation. Our hero gave it to the torturers. The pain they caused grew <hero_name>'s power.
The torturers cackle at the sight of the Poppet. You hand it to them, the pain they cause with it feeds the Rot within you.
"I know this place."
The Stranger knew the layout of the chambers, and lead our hero through them. How he knew, these halls <hero_name> dared not ask.
The Stranger, eyes distant, leads you through a set of back passages to a special observation room. The King's. From it, you syphon power.
"These are free beasts."
Our hero freed the prisoners with the Royal Pardon. <hero_name> cared not for their thanks. The King was weaker, that's what mattered.
The Royal Pardon excuses each and every prisoner. With one of the King's power sources gone, he will be weakened in the final battle.
Usually reserved for the King's enemies, the prison in <quest_tile> is filled with the innocent. The lead torturer growls at your approach.
Our hero journeyed to <quest_tile>. Deep within the dungeon, screams echoed up. The King's agents were hard at work.
<hero_name> heard rumour that the King now fed upon the suffering his torturers caused. Foiling them might weaken him.
Innocent beasts are being tortured by the King. It's said that their pain feeds his dark power. Perhaps you can use this to your advantage.
Eye for an Eye
Volunteer as Conduit
Our hero volunteered as conduit, but the surge of power was too great. It damaged their spirit, leaving them weak, and angry.
You are surrounded by chanting cultists. Together, they channel magic through you. You howl. It's too much! The world goes black.
Our hero volunteered as conduit for the Ritual. It worked. The spell shot Rot across the land, and grew our hero's power.
It begins to rain as the ritual begins. Dozens of cultists channel their power into you. Rot boils in your belly. You smile. Awakened.
Join the ritual
The chosen acolyte could not withstand the power, and fell to pure Rot. Still, our hero learnt much of the dark magic's potential power.
You join the cultists, and channel the power of your Rot through the chosen acolyte. Their body cannot withstand the force. They perish.
"Let be bind the conduit down."
The Blacksmith did not trust the strange magics of the Ritual. They secured the conduit with manacles, an action which saved their life.
The Blacksmith prepares the chosen acolyte with chains and long manacles. The bindings stop them from harming themselves. The spell is cast.
"Let me prepare the spell."
Our hero's Apprentice prepared the spell. "These cultists are amateurs." He scoffed, then stood back. "There, ready."
The Apprentice has prepared a thousand rituals for his master. He readies <quest_tile> for the spell. "There. Now it will work."
"I'll do it."
The Brilliant Fool volunteered as conduit, and survived the process. From that day forth, he was never quite as jovial.
You almost stop the Brilliant Fool from volunteering, then shrug. To your amazement, he survives. The spell is a success.
Disciples of darkness stride about the plain. The spell is almost ready. The Rot will be proliferated. All that is needed is a conduit.
The tools of darkness were spread about. Rabbit paws, goblets of blood. The spell was almost complete, but needed someone to channel it.
Followers of darkness from around Armello were gathering secretly in <quest_tile>. A spell was to be cast, one our hero had a stake in.
Cultists call for disciples. A spell to spread Rot is ready to be cast. Those who help, will be blessed with power.
A Dark Pact
Excavate the tomb
The darkness underground eluded our hero. They dug for hours, but the Rot Queen had been buried too deep. Our hero left, angry.
You want that power. For hours you toil, shifting dirt, but tire quickly. Finally, you stagger away. A mocking laugh echoes on the wind.
As <hero_name> struck the dead queen's bones, a terrible wind flew forth from the grave. It was the queen's power. Our hero took it.
You dig for hours with single minded determination. Finally, you strike bone. A howling wind bursts from the grave, flowing into you.
Offer Prayer
Such power that the very land is corrupted around your tomb. Our hero was impressed, and payed their respects.
Worship is not natural to the corrupted. You acknowledge the power this beast held... and promise not to make the same mistakes she did.
"Let me tell the story of this Queen."
The Bard told the story of the dark Queen as our hero sat before the crypt. They learnt many lessons from the tale of her death.
You sit before the tomb. The Bard's gentle voice carries you off to a different time. The lessons of the past give you plans for the future.
"Let me map this land."
Maps of untamed places, such as a legendary tomb, can fetch a pretty sum. Our hero's explorer drew one up, and split the value with our hero.
The explorer, stares at the crypt. Amazed. They produce a chart and begin mapping the area. You split the value of its sale.
"I'll dig it up in half a second!"
The tomb released it's magic all at once, hitting our hero's Berserker. Luckily, <hero_name> absorbed some of the errant magic.
The Berserker's massive arms strain as he frantically digs. The tomb releases a blast of magic, which hits him, but you sap some of it away.
The swamp stinks, but you enter anyway. The Rot emanates from the tomb of an old Wolven Queen. Power radiates from the crypt.\n
Deep within the stinking mire, our hero discovered the source of the Rot taint. The ancient tomb of a dark Queen. Abandoned and long forgotten.
<hero_name> knew <quest_tile> was cursed by Rot. Supposedly, if the source of darkness within could be found, it's power could be harnessed.
The Rot will never fade from Armello. It is intrinsic. Certain lands are tainted with it. Within these places, one can find great power.
The Pillar of Rot
Hunt for the King's Blood
Our hero let slip that they were searching for a drop or two or Royal Blood. Unfortunately, the wrong ears heard, and let the King know.
You haven't the skill to keep your search secret. Word spreads like wyldfyre. The King's agents hear, and rally to teach you a lesson.
The blood was easy enough to come by. Upon drinking it, our hero felt the darkness within them grow stronger. Their time was coming.
You're careful who you trust. You plot with a servant, and, somehow... they get a single drop. You slay them. No witnesses.
Gather Bane's Blood
Our hero gathered the Bane blood, completed the ritual and drank deep. Sadly, it would seem that the darkness gathered wasn't strong enough.
You've dealt with more Banes than you can count. Wounding a few and gathering their blood is nothing, but the spell seems ineffective.
"I can get what you need."
The Spymaster can get their paws on anything. They managed to conjure up a drop of diluted King's blood. The Wyld alone knows how.
The Spymaster speaks with her contacts. A single drop of the King's blood is soon acquired, though it has been diluted, and lost some power.
"I can find a way to buy it."
Enough coin will get you anything. <hero_name>'s trader organised a grey market deal. The blood came about, but it's magic was weak.
Your trader nods. "Everything can be brought, at a price."  He somehow trades for the blood, but the act of purchase weakens the dark magic.
"I can make a better potion with one hand."
Our hero's Alchemist could not abide the amateur alchemy of the cultists. They stepped in, and brewed a more potent potion.
The Alchemist scoffs at the cultist's ways. Using their ingredients (which you... borrow for him) He creates a potion that strengthens your magic.
The rumours are true. The cultists of <quest_tile> explain the magic behind their spell. The more corrupted the being, the better.
Drinking another beast's blood isn't strange. The wild ones still hunt travelers. But when combined with ritual, the deed has unholy powers.
<hero_name> heard rumour of a group of cultists drinking Bane blood to deepen their connection with the Rot.
It's said that a group of Rot cultists have been drinking the blood of the corrupted to increase their power.
Bane Blood
Force through the fog.
The coils of fog snaked around our hero's neck. <hero_name> only just managed to drag themselves away to safety, injured, but alive.
Your very life is choked away by the coiling mist. You fall to your knees. You only just manage to crawl away to saftey.
<hero_name> forced on, drew their weapon and approached the scientist's lair. Their research proved useful, and their screams soothing.
You spit out a curse. You will not fall! You break though. The fog fades, revealing the scientist's lair. You snarl and approach.
Retreat and plan your attack
<hero_name> retreated and observed, learning the ways of the mist. They finally found a way through, but by then, the scientist had fled.
You flee the mist and take shelter nearby. You eventually spot a safe path and use it, but the delay lets the scientist flee.
Leap! Now!"
The cloying fingers of mist dispersed at the Winged Boot's leap. Sadly, they overshoot their mark, and the scientist had time to flee.
The Winged Boots launch you from the fog's clutches and out of the valley. It takes time to return. By the time you do, the scientist has fled.
Cut through the mist.
Our hero's Moon Scythe was the answer. It cut through the mist, but the time it took let the scientist escape.
The Moon Scythe parts the choking fog with its shining blade. But it takes time. The scientist is given time to flee.
Don the Helm of Heroes.
Our hero was protected by the Helm of Heroes, but their quest was for naught. The journey through the fog gave the scientist time to flee.
The Helm of Heroes keeps the fog from your eyes and neck. Though it tears at you, you force on, only to find the scientist's lair empty.
A sinister mist coats the valley. As you pass through it, it tightens around your neck. An ambush! The wizard controls the mist!
As our hero approached the scientist's lair, they passed through a barrier of shimmering fog. It came to life! An attack!
Our hero heard word of a Mad Rot Scientist, hiding in Deeppaw Valley, in southern <quest_tile>. Their "research" could prove useful.
Stay away from the Deeppaw valley. Some kind of Rot wizard has set up there, and kidnaps travelers to fuel his "research".
Valley of the Twisting Mist
Fight with skill alone
After hours of battle, our hero suspected a stalemate, but then the she bear revealed her true strength. Our hero only just escaped.
You duel for hours. Intense, quick combat. Suddenly she scoffs. "I'm bored." She disarms and wounds you with ease. "You're weak."
The two beasts struggled until at last <hero_name> won with a stab to the gut. The bear's Rot seeped from the wound. Our hero stole it.
Her blade shines as yours clashes against it. The duel lasts hours, but you're the more skilled. You knock her sword aside and cut her down.
Use the Rot to bolster your strength.
Our hero sapped the Rot strength from the she bear. As she collapsed to one knee, <hero_name> unleashed her power. A single strike was enough.
She has martial skill, but you are the master of the Rot. You draw her strength from her, and fell her with a mighty strike.
Open fire.
Pride and Victory feeds the Rot in amateurs, But a master knows the importance of practicality. <hero_name> shot Liana down with the Hand Cannons.
No time for petty duels. You bring the she bear down in a hail of shots. Her body yields a useful treasure.
Approach Carefully.
Liana rained down strike after strike, but they were deflected by the strength of the Royal Shield. Our hero cut her down. Victory.
Hidden behind the Royal Shield, you approach carefully. The bear's strikes ring as they hit your shield, but none wound you. You cut her down.
Grasp the Wyldfyre staff.
Our hero's connection with the Wyld was... tense, but the Wyldfyre staff was still an effective weapon against Liana.
You can no longer rely on the staff's magic, but it's an effective weapon. Its reach protects you. The she bear flees, cursing your name.
You spot the she bear standing watch on the crest of a hill. Her eyes glow black with the Rot's power. "I challenge you." She shouts.
Liana was once a mighty warrior. <hero_name> had heard tales of her. The husk before them was half of what she was, but twice as deadly.
<hero_name> heard word of a corrupted soldier decimating travellers in <quest_tile>. Our hero journeyed forth to steal her strength.
A mighty warrior, corrupted by the Rot, has been challenging passing travellers. If you can slay her, her power shall be yours.
Duelists of Rot
Plant the seeds of discord
But our hero did not have the wit for subtlety. Their words fell on deaf ears. The peasants would not feed the Rot. What fools.
You whisper lies and try to turn beast against beast, but the blasted creatures are too amicable. You leave grumpily. Stupid happy peasants.
Our hero had mastered the ways of lies. They soaked in the village's misery, then turned it to anger against the King before they left.
At the power of your whispers, neighbour turns against neighbour. Petty squabbles grow catastrophic. You stay in the village, soaking in the sadness.
Threaten the villagers
Or not... <hero_name> threatened the people, hoping their fear would feed our hero's power. They fled before it could.
The villagers are terrified at the sight of you, and even more so when you threaten their lives. They pack up and flee before you can bask in their misery.
Use the Masquerade Mask
The grotesque visage of the Masquerade Mask was enough to terrify the villagers. The fear fed the Rot within our hero.
Your words are like a phantom's. You terrify the people, but many of them are so scared they flee. Still, the fear feeds you... somewhat.
Our hero had mastered the ways of lies. They soaked in the village's misery, then turned it to anger against the King before they left.
At the power of your whispers, neighbour turns against neighbour. Petty squabbles grow catastrophic. You stay in the village, soaking in the sadness.
"I can cause terror."
Our hero's conjurer took it upon themselves to cause the fear. Their parlour magic provided much for <hero_name> to feed upon.
The conjurer creates illusions of twisting shadows and dark creatures. The villagers flee, terrified. Their screams feed your power.
Create Illusions
Stories of the "Dancing Lights" are still told around <quest_tile> today. But it was merely our hero, and their Mirror Cape, causing fear.
Commoners fear magic like the fools they are. You use the mirror cape to cause strange flashes and lights. Their fear bolsters your strength.
The peaceful village of <quest_tile> is spread before you. No violence is needed here. Deceit and lies will cause the darkness you seek.
Our hero arrived at <quest_tile> unsure. They knew that they needed to cause fear, but by banditry or attack? No. Something subtler...
Our hero was newly corrupted, and knew of a few ways to grow their power. They were drawn to chaos, so decided to cause some.
Dissent and distrust feeds the power within you. Corrupting a settlement would create Rot. Rot which you could surely syphon.
A Disturbing Thought
Help summon the Bane
Our hero overestimated their connection with the Rot. When they tried to summon the Bane, the magic struck them down.
You raise a paw towards the focus of the Rot. A screech fills the air. The Rot strikes back with a bolt of magic. You fall, wounded.
The ground bubbled with foul black ichor. From within the pure Rot, the Bane emerged. Beautiful and glorious in sin.
The darkness grows. A gout of Rot explodes into the air, and the great Bane emerges. It shrieks, then takes flight, soaring away.
Drain the Rot power
The raw magic in the air was too tempting to resist. Our hero syphoned it into their own spirit, claiming the power for themselves.
You have no interest in creating a Bane. This power will serve. You drain it away, strengthening the magic within you.
"Together we can summon it!"
Our hero was practically a Warlock within their own right. Together with their companion, they summoned the terrible Bane.
The Warlock's eyes are wide with excitement. Together, you bring the Bane forth. Its power surges through the both of you.
The mountain is shadowed. Sickness hangs in the air. Atop the peak a point in the sky flickers with purple light. Something is wrong.
Though the magic had begun, the Bane had not appeared. Something was wrong. The creature was not forming.
Our hero heard rumour of a Bane forming on the peak of <quest_tile>. Watching this birth might teach much of the Rot's ways.
See those dark clouds? You mark my words. A Bane is forming there. It will come into being any day now.
The Miracle of Birth
Order the beast to kneel
Our hero's power over the Rot had not reached its peak. They were unable to command the Bane's loyalty, and it dealt them a terrible wound.
Flee? Perhaps... but the Bane would not kneel to <hero_name>. It feigned submission, then attacked, wounding our hero grievously.
Our hero subdued the Bane, making it kneel before them. This first success was great, but tiring. The skill needed more training.
The Bane screeches. Once, twice, then finally goes silent. It folds its wings and kneels. You smile. You are truely the master of the Rot.
Order the beast to flee.
Our hero used the power of the Rot to affect the beast. It fled, though through fear or compulsion, <hero_name> did not know.
The Rot surges within you, you cry and force the Beast back. At last, it flees, but you're not sure if it was simply afraid, or compelled to.
Prepare beforehand
Our hero's spell failed, and the Bane attacked. Fortunately <hero_name> was prepared. The strike glanced off the Lionheart Breastplate.
Aware of the danger you're in, you don the Lionheart Breastplate. Your spell fails, but the beast's attacks glance off you. You flee, quickly.
"I... will... serve..."
Though the Bane was unaffected, <hero_name>'s will affected their squire. Devotion and loyalty can be combined with magic, it seems.
You widen your eyes. The Squire, next to you seems dazed. It would seem that the Rot has power over the uncorrupted as well.
The Bane leaps to attack!
Our hero was attacked before they could begin to cast the spell, but the Bane's Blade leapt up, shielding them. Just in time.
And your Bane's Blade parries its strike just in time. You kick it back and cut it down. Lucky. It would seem you need a little more practice.
The locals point you towards a Bane hidden within an abandoned warren by a river. You enter. The beast screeches at the sight of you.
Our hero tracked the bane to the depths of a riverside warren. It was time to see if the rumours were true, and the beasts could be commanded.
Rot Lords can command Banes, and the King was trying to do so. Our hero vowed to learn how first, and ventured to <quest_tile> to find one.
It seems the King is studying how to command the loyalty of Banes. Supposedly, powerful Rot Lords have sway over the beasts.\n
Dark Leader
Don the crown.
The burden on the body of the wounded was too great for <hero_name> to withstand. The ritual failed. Our hero was hurt.
You are not ready for this power. Within moments you begin to scream. Your eyes bleed. You rip off the crown and flee, whimpering.
Our hero withstood the magic of the dark crown. The Rot within them was strengthened. When <hero_name> took the throne, they'd keep that crown.
The crown feels like burning iron upon your brow. You howl, but fury forces you through the pain. Soon, it subsides. Your power grows.
Draw power from the Crown
Our hero could not risk the injury of the trial. Instead they shattered the relic, then drew the power it contained into themselves.
Shattering the delicate relic causes its magic to leak out. You seize upon it, drawing its power into your own body.
"Let me perform the procedure."
Our hero had the Apothecary perform the ritual upon them. It garnered them a meagre amount of power for their quest.
The Apothecary runs the ritual like a surgical operation. The perfectionism weakens the magic, but lessens the risk.
Harness the Rot within the crown.
Our hero used the Bane's Claw, to harness the Rot within the relic. The claw was both a tool of good and evil. As was our hero.
The Bane's Claw makes the crown shimmer. The malevolent power fades into the claw. You will put it to good use.
You "retrieve" the crown without issue. Going over Eden's notes, you find that those who can endure wearing the crown, grow in power.
Eden's notes on the artifact, a strange, black crown, were simple. Wounds it inflicted would proliferate the wearer's Rot.
Eden, a fabled Rat Clan explorer, had found an ancient Rot crown deep within a dungeon. Our hero journeyed to <quest_tile> to find him.
A treasure hunter came across a Rot cursed treasure in the depths of a nearby dungeon. Its power might be useful.
Crown of Rotted Thought
Extend your claws
Our hero attempted to do battle with the soothsayer, but was overcome by the strength of their Wyldself.
You lack the same connection with your Wyldself. The soothsayer cuts you deep, and you flee, injured and ashamed.
Our hero needed no Wyldself, they were one with the Rot. They channeled the power of its chaos, and overcame the soothsayer.
The soothsayer may claw with Wyld, but you tear with rot. Primal and savage, you rip at each other. You bite his throat and drink the blood.
Cut him down
Our hero had not the power to fight against their Wyldself. Instead, they smashed the Mirror Lake. They let the Wyld's power fade.
The way of beasts is no match for a good weapon. You'll not lower yourself to his terms. You kill the soothsayer. The Rot will spread unhindered.
Raise the Wyld Talisman
Our hero used the distraction of the Wyld talisman to camouflage their attack. What fools the beings of Wyld were.
The Spirit's eyes soften at the sight of the talisman. That's all the distraction you need. You attack. The spirit falls back into the lake.
Corrupt your Wyldself
Our hero could not overcome their Wyldself, but they could do damage. They corrupted the spirit with the Raven's Beak dagger.
You can't slay your own spirit, but you can weaken it! You strike with the Raven's Beak Dagger, the spirit shrieks, as the Rot corrupts it.
Show the Royal Banner
Our hero convinced the spirit to cooperate by reminding them of the true enemy. The Mad King, and his torturous ways.
You plant the banner down. "Let's not forget the real enemy. Stay out of my way until Armello is safe." Your Wyldself nods.
The soothsayer stands as you arrive. "I don't need my sight to know you intentions." He kneels, then unleashes his Wyldself, roaring loud.
The soothsayer sensed <hero_name>'s arrival. They extend their claws. Ready to battle as beasts did in the old days.
The Wyldself is an ancient art, where one comes in touch with their primal self. Doing so, heals Rot, something our hero could not allow.
A blind monk has been healing the corrupted with an ancient druidic technique called "The Wyldself." Stop the damage he's doing.
The Wyldself
Hunt for the Glade's Location
Our hero hunted through the tomes for hours, but found nothing. The rambling notes of the monks were nothing more than a petty distraction.
You study until the candles burn low and your eyelids droop. Finally, frustrated, you slam the books shut and leave. A waste of time.
As our hero gave up on the tomes, they felt the tingle of magic. Soon, they found the Rot Glade, locked away below the temple.
The books are useless, but you sense something. You search the temple, and find a staircase leading to an underground garden. You smile.
Learn more of the Rot
The Rot has been studied for aeons. It has always been part of Armello. Our hero learnt much of its ways from the monks' books.
No time to chase fairy tales. You raid the monastery's books on dealing with the Rot. You learn much of its use in ancient times.
"There's too much treasure to resist."
Our hero soon gave up the search. Their Miner was making too much noise prying gems from the monastery. At least they would fetch a good price.
Your Miner raises their pick and begins striking loose gems inlaid in the walls. The constant ringing makes it impossible to concentrate.
"I can help you know..."
Our hero's Coin Master spent their life hovering over ledgers. They helped our hero search for valuable information.
Years of searching for one transaction among thousands makes the Coin Master perfect for this job. They find many useful tidbits about the Rot.
The temple on <quest_tile> is home to many tomes of the Rot arts. You break in, then study the dusty scrolls.
The monks at <quest_tile> were no problem. Our hero cut down those that refused them entry. Then begin their search for mention of the glade.\n
Our hero heard rumour of a "Rot Glade". An ancient site imbued with power. They journeyed to the library at <quest_tile> to learn more.
A monk order's legends tells of an ancient site, imbued with the Rot. The power it contains must be unthinkable.
The Rot Glade
Accept the Palace's invitation.
Our hero followed the path. The rotten core of Armello drew them in. The palace was coated in thorns. They parted for <hero_name>.
You've changed on your journey, the darkness embracing you. Now... you are ready to lead all Armello through this same change.
Thorns rip apart the palace walls to let you through. As you pass the fountains the water turns to black ichor. The palace welcomes you home.
The wind was cold as it whipped through the palace. Black ichor burned a path for <hero_name>. A carpet of dark lead towards the king.
The Rot had chosen a new champion. <hero_name> would strike down the false king.  The Rot's true disciple would herald in new age.
The grass dies as you tread upon it. The Wyld will not approach you. You are becometh Rot. You're ready. The palace awaits.
Death to the King
STORY BONUS
Challenge Reward
Prove yourself. Attack!
Our hero had tasted their first challenge, and been defeated. The journey hadn't started well. But <hero_name> was determined.
You don't even have time to draw your weapon. You're leapt on, beaten bloody and tossed outside. "You'll never make it to the throne."
Just as they were about to spring into battle, <hero_name>'s attacker knelt. The attack had been a test. Our hero was worthy.
You charge. Mid fight, your opponent yields. "I mean no harm! I needed to be sure you're worthy of my loyalty. Let me join your quest!"
Flee the inn
<hero_name> fled like a frightened pup. Our hero's face burnt as they ran. This could not stand. They would not flee again.\n
You turn. Sprint through the city streets. The figure gives chase. You lose him in the twisting alleys. You spend the night hidden. Afraid.
The inn is dark. Empty. As you enter a figure strides forth from the shadow. The sound of ringing steel echoes. It's a trap!
<hero_name> knew the race for Armello's throne was sure to be filled with peril, but was not prepared for an ambush at the meet.
Word of <hero_name>'s approach had moved quicker than expected. Word had it, somebody hoped to meet with our hero at <quest_tile> inn.
"You're <hero_name>! The one they've been talking about. Someone's been looking for you."
A First Test
Take them all on at once
<hero_name> took on the whole forest. Their pride proved a hindrance. They were wounded in the battle and only just snatched victory.
The ruffians swarm you from every direction. There are more than you thought. You see you overestimated your skill, and are forced to flee.
<hero_name> stormed the forest and cleared it of bandits, but the land would not be truly safe until the Mad King's rule ended.
No lowly thief will overcome you, no matter how many try. You clear the forest, and help yourself to the thieves' treasure stash.
Eliminate the thieves with stealth
<hero_name> crept through the thicket, slaying the thieves on by one. Cruelty and banditry could not be tolerated in Armello.
You creep through the forest, and lay waste to the thieve's camps. The forest is safe once again.
<quest_tile> has been turned into a den of thieves. Their camps stretch to every corner of the woods..
The thieves had overtaken the forest. Without a hero to clear them out, the surrounding towns would be in dire peril.
Armello has become a dark and dangerous place. <hero_name> agreed to help restore peace by hunting thieves hiding in <quest_tile>.
The King's Guard have failed in their duty to keep the land safe from bandits and thieves. Someone needs to take up arms.
Pruning Weeds
Attack the Troll
<hero_name> did not have the creature's natural affinity with the stinking bog. The beast wounded our hero, and escaped.
As you charge the beast your foot slips on the muddy bank. The troll, at home in the swamp, wounds you and escapes.
The troll was bigger and stronger, but <hero_name> was the better fighter. The beast was slain, and our hero claimed its Spirit Stone.
You wake the troll with a shout, then leap forward and attack. The fight is fierce, but you emerge victorious, and claim the beast's Spirit Stone.
Rob the creature
<hero_name> approached with caution, stealing the Spirit Stone without the troll being any the wiser.
The troll might hold the stone close, but it's other goods are scattered around haphazardly. You liberate a few, and leave, grinning.
You can't tell what smells worse in <quest_tile> the mud, or the troll. The creature is asleep, half covered in filthy water.
The troll was dozing in one of the festering pools. <hero_name> could see the Spirit Stone clutched in its grubby paw.
Trolls, rare and dangerous creatures, love shiny goods. A particularly large one had stolen a Spirit Stone and was hiding in <quest_tile>.
A wicked troll has stolen a Spirit Stone from a nearby monastery. Whoever slays the beast is welcome to keep it.
Troll Treasure
Cure the well with the Wyld's power
<hero_name> tried to use the Wyld to cure the rot infestation. It had no effect. The task was beyond our hero.
You are still a novice in the ways of the Wyld. The well will not heal. The attempt leaves you weakened. The village is beyond help.
<hero_name> cured the well's water, and the Wyld rewarded them with a Spirit Stone. With time, perhaps the villagers would be healed as well.
Mist rises from the well, boiling out and filling the streets. The villagers seem to calm. A spirit stone bobs to the water's surface.
Burn the village
Our hero was forced to take the dark path. <hero_name> purged the settlement. A foul necessity.
A hero is sometimes called upon to take the dark route. There was no other way. You destroy the rot, and the town.
Inside the village you find the source of the rot madness. The village well is corrupted by thick purple veins of rot.
The people of <quest_tile> had been swayed by the Rot magic, emanating from the corrupted well. They were a danger to themselves and others.
Another settlement had fallen to the darkness of the rot. Surrounding Armellians are under threat. It must be purged.
The rot has taken ahold of a nearby settlement. The folk inside have been driven mad. There's no hope for them.
Rot Land
Debate the law
The treacherous coin masters, stalled <hero_name>'s quest with legal games. A setback for sure, but our hero would not be dissuaded.
You stammer out a defence. The slimy solicitors laugh at your words. They pervert the law, draining you of resources for your quest.
Whoever thought the Wolf Clan had not the wits to fight with words would nurse their purse that night. <hero_name> won, and gained an ally.
You trap the coin masters in legal jargon, and have them return to the palace. In thanks, the village leader joins your cause.
Intimidate the tax masters
<hero_name> would not let their quest be stalled by the king's representatives. The King would see him in person soon enough.
You slam your fist down on the table. One leg collapses. The tax masters scurry away. You snort. So be it. None of these games.
The very air in <quest_tile> seems grey. The King's coin masters are set up in the village square, counting their ill gotten gold.
The Mad King's tax collector had made themselves comfortable. They were bleeding the wolves of <quest_tile> dry.
The King's servants are taxing the Wolf Clan. Blood and steel is dangerous, but legal games could stall <hero_name>'s quest just as easily.
Extra taxes have been levied on the Wolf Clan. The huge cost could stop any support for <hero_name>.
Mightier than the Pen
Sneak in and steal the treasure!
Our hero leapt into action, but was not as fleet as they first thought. They were discovered and forced to flee in shame.
You scale the museum wall. Halfway up your handholds give way. You fall into the middle of the crowd. Humiliated more than hurt, you flee.
<hero_name> stole into the museum and took the treasure. Our hero escaped quickly, more dangerous than before.
Through the shadows, up the wall, into the museum. Before the guards realise the treasure is gone, you're far, far away.
Garner support from the crowd
The artifact was too well guarded. Rather than risk being caught, <hero_name> took the opportunity to gather supporters.
Rather than steal, you use the time at the opening to gather support from the dignitaries present. You learn much of clan politics.
Patrons sip hot rot wine and discuss art around the entrance. The gates are not yet open, and guards surround the building.
A party to celebrate the opening was in full swing. <hero_name> couldn't get close to the building, let alone the artifact.
<hero_name> heard word of a great treasure being revealed at <quest_tile> museum. Our hero decided to... liberate it. For the cause.
A party is being held for the unveiling of a valuable artifact at a newly opened museum.
Wolf Burglar
Rely on your preparation. Continue on
Smarts only get you so far. <hero_name>'s lesson learned, Our hero resolved to pay more heed to their surroundings
Relying on the time you spent preparing equipment, you venture on. Hours later, freezing and exhausted, you find yourself back at the mountain's base.
Forcing through the storm's fury, blinded and freezing, our hero finally found the stone, and ended its grip over the mountain.
Snow is no danger to the well prepared. Snug within your thick cloak, you continue on, and find the Spirit Stone.
Hunker down. Survive the storm.
The storm was too powerful to continue. <hero_name> fled, escaping the winter fury to the safety of the mountain's base.
Wolves know how to deal with cold. You forge a snow cave and curl up in your bedroll. You retreat next morning during a break in the snow.
As you begin the climb, the sky turns dark. Soon, the worst storm you've ever seen rages around you. Snow and sleet blocks your vision.
The stone's magic was seeping into the mountain. A storm was brewing, and <hero_name> was trapped within it!
Stories in the inns and around the campfire, told of an ancient Spirit Stone, high up on the peaks of <quest_tile>.
"I've heard rumbling from the mountain. I bet it's one of those Spirit Stones, wreaking havoc with the weather."
Blind-Sight
Ask for the riddle
The riddle was as foolish as the creature who ran it. <hero_name> left disgruntled, strangely weakened by the ordeal.
The goat opens his mouth. Instead of words, strange sounds emerge. The goat sees your confusion and shakes his head. "You've failed."
The goat spoke in the ancient Wyld tongue, which our hero was able to decypher. The goat bestowed a treasure upon them as reward.
"Do you speak the Wyld?" The goats voice is deep and fearsome. You answer "Yes." The goat smiles. He hands over the treasure.
Ask for the blessing
<hero_name> asked for the blessing. The goat whispered into our hero's ear, and the Wyld renewed their strength.
The goat nods. "Caution is wisdom my friend." He leans forward and whispers into your ear. You feel your strength renewed.
In the middle of the grasses of <quest_tile>, sits a blind goat. "I offer two things. A riddle, or a blessing."
The blind goat sat alone in the waving grass of <quest_tile>. He offered our hero two things, a riddle, or a blessing.
A stranger in Armello had devised the ultimate riddle. He was offering a mystical treasure as a reward for whoever solved it.
A crazed wanderer is offering a powerful treasure to whomever can solve his riddle.
Old Games
Counter his magic with the Wyld
<hero_name> called the Wyld, but it would not respond. The malevolent warlock cursed our hero, poisoning him with Rot.
Your cry to the Wyld goes unanswered. As you hesitate, confused, the warlock moves his spell to you. You feel the Rot flood your veins.
With the Wyld's help, <hero_name> was able to save the stranger from the warlock. In thanks, they swore themselves to our hero.
Wind rushes into the village. The warlock shudders at the Wyld's touch. He flees. The stranger, freed from his clutches, swears to you.
Alert the villagers
<hero_name> rallied the villagers against the warlock. He fled, tail between his legs. Leaving the settlement safe once more.
You point out the warlock and rally the villagers to action. Together, you chase the warlock from the village, foiling his plot.
The celebrations are glorious. Just as you relax, you spot one of the king's magus. They're whispering a spell of rot at a passing stranger.
The festival was indeed spoiled by dark magic. A Rot warlock was whispering into the ear of a passing stranger, a spell of corruption.
The Mad King's mages were infiltrating public festivals and corrupting Armellians with rot. <hero_name> was forced to step up.
The Mad King has been hosting lavish festivals. His mages are using the gatherings to infect the innocent with Rot.
No Rest for the Wolves
Spin around, weapon at the ready.
Alas, no plan prepared our hero for the axe thrown from the bushes! As our hero howled in pain, the bandit fox fled in victory.
You turn, but the only trace of your pursuer is an axe that bites into your leg. Its owner cackles maniacally and flees into the forest.
Lying in wait, our hero was more than ready to deflect the assassin's axe. The black fox fled, leaving behind a Spirit Stone.
You spin and deftly strike at an incoming axe! Its owner, a black fox, is quick to flee, but not before dropping her satchel.
Lose your pursuer in the forest.
The dark forest was a perfect place to lose an unwanted pursuer. Our hero ducked and weaved for hours, and the tail was soon lost for good.
The chase lasts far longer than you would have expected, but in the end you lose them. You're stronger than you knew.
Don the Helmet of Heroes for extra protection.
No sooner did our hero don the fabled helm did a thrown axe strike it! The bandit fox begged for leniency, offering a reward in exchange.
The moment you don the helm, an axe bounces harmlessly off its tough exterior. The bandit pleads for mercy, offering a reward in exchange.
Use the Squire as bait
The squire served as an excellent distraction, allowing <hero_name> to overcome the assassin. The squire survived, luckily.
You place your cloak upon on the squire's shoulders. When the assassin attacks, you charge her. She bargains for her life with treasure.
Fool your attacker
Using the Mirror Cape to disorientate their pursuer, our hero overcame the assassin. They would have to try harder to fool <hero_name>.\n
Using the Mirror Cape you disorientate your pursuer and slip behind them. At dagger point, they bargain for their live with treasure.
You push onward, deep into the forest, then double back on your footprints, lying in wait. Suddenly, there is a rustling in the bushes...
Try as they did, our hero was unable to shake the follower. In a nearby forest, <hero_name> concocted a plan.
<hero_name> had barely begun questing for the throne when a strange follower seemed to materialise from nowhere...
Don't look now, but you seem to have an unwelcome follower on your tracks. Might want to try and lose them in that nearby forest.
The Obsidian Fox
Challenge the fool to a mead-drinking contest.
Alas, nobody could best that boar in a mead-drinking contest! Our legendary hero would wake up the next morning with a legendary headache!
You make it through two mugs of the sweet wine, but lack the fortitude to continue. "Give me one more!" You yell, before passing out.
Indeed, the boar was shocked when a wolf bested him in his own mead hall! "You are worthy of my respect," he said. "One more for the road!"
While your physical training was never intended for such things, you best the boar in his own mead hall, gaining his profound respect.
A contest of steel is the only solution here.
But our hero had no time for games! With a flash of steel, the oaf hastily recanted his words. Whether he meant it or not, we'll never know.
You won't play this fool's game. In an instant, your blade flashes and the boar relents -- though you doubt his loyalty is absolute.
"As your doctor I cannot advise this. Then again..."
A simple tonic from <hero_name>'s loyal doctor helped guarantee success, the boar's respect, and a legendary headache to boot!
The doctor offers a simple brew to help keep the mead from sapping your wits. You earn the boar's respect, along with a pounding headache!
"I'm sure we can come to a more profitable arrangement."
<hero_name>'s coinmaster was well versed in the devious ways of nobility. He secured the baron's support, sipping mead as he did it.
At the mention of coin, the baron's eyes light up. Your coin master slides out a chair and sits. "There's profit here for everyone."
Use the Poppet to cheat
Our hero used the poppet doll to tip the odds in their favour. The baron passed out within minutes. <hero_name> was the victor.
The poppet doll is perfect for this. You spill your mead upon it. Soon, the baron is a snoring mess, while you leave, your wits still sharp.
The massive boar invites you into his prized mead hall. "I'll stop the insults if you can prove you have strength to lead! What'll it be?"
The boar's mead hall would be the proving ground for the Wolf Clan. The boar baron had the advantage, but <hero_name> was determined to win!
The rumors were vicious: a boar baron in a nearby town was calling <hero_name> a coward and weakling. Clearly that couldn't continue!
Wolf Clan honor could be at stake! Word is the baron of a nearby village is calling you a weakling and a coward. Best put a stop to that!
The Mead Hall
Pull the wagon free.
Our hero tried in vain to pull the wagon free, but such strength was beyond <hero_name>. The merchant and wagon would never leave the swamp.
You pull and pull, but you simply lack the strength. The merchant and his wagon are soon sucked under the muck, never to be seen again.
With the legendary strength of the Wolf Clan, <hero_name> pulled the wagon from the grime single-pawed! The caravan was saved!
The merchant cannot believe his eyes as you successfully drag the wagon to solid ground. The prize he offers was well worth the effort!
Help the merchant, leave the caravan.
Our hero could not save both the merchant and his treasures. The dog accepted <hero_name>'s help, but lost his fortune in an instant.
"Leave the wagon," you yell. "I can't save both!" The dog accepts your help, but is despondent nonetheless -- his wealth is gone forever.
Why despair when one can take flight with Winged Boots?
Still, even with limited options, a pair of Winged Boots would serve the situation well! Our hero saved both merchant and caravan with ease.
The Winged Boots provide you with a simple solution to this problem. The merchant and his goods are safe, and your paws aren't even dirty!
"Put your back into it! Come on!"
Stinking mud and heavy wagons were lighter than the blacksmith's forge hammer. He ripped the wagon out of the mire. Saving the dog.
Your blacksmith leaps down into the stinking mud. With mighty heave, he drags the wagon free. The dog gives you both a gift in thanks.
You find the wagon deep in the mire, still sinking. The dog merchant pleads with you for help, but your options are tragically limited.
And there, deep in the mire, the wagon lay half-consumed by the muck. "Help me!" The dog merchant pleaded. But what could be done?
The caravan was late, that much was known. Our hero suspected it had foolishly tried to cut through <quest_tile>.
We were expecting a caravan to pass by here yesterday, but it hasn't yet arrived. I fear they may be trapped in <quest_tile>!
The Sinking Caravan
You're strong enough! Force your way through the cold.
<hero_name> pushed onward, but the nefarious magic proved too strong, the cold too brutal. Our hero fled, leaving the others to their fate.
You push on, but the cold saps your strength in an instant. Barely conscious, you flee the mountain and leave the others to their fate.
<hero_name> struggled against the storm, ultimately confronting the warlock in a flurry of steel. She fell, and the travelers were saved!
You push forward, relying on strength alone. "How did you-!" The warlock never finishes her words of surprise -- your blade ends her life.
Take shelter from the warlock's magic.
Our hero waited for the mage to exhaust her magic, felling her with ease. Sadly, the other explorers on the mountain perished in the storm.
You wait for the warlock's magic to dissipate in a nearby cave, making her an easy foe. Unfortunately, the other explorers are not so lucky.
Fight Rot with Rot
The Rot can never be trusted, and often forsakes its own. The Raven Beak's Dagger lead our hero to the warlock. She fell quickly.
The Raven's Beak dagger hums when pointed north. You follow its call through blinding snow. Soon, you reach the Warlock. She's an easy kill.
"Fool the Warlock with the Masquerade Mask"
The devious Masquerade Mask duped the foolish warlock. Thinking she recognized her own, she halted the storm, letting <hero_name> attack!
Donning the mask gives you the appearance of a fellow Rot worshiper. The Warlock slows the storm for you, letting you reach and slay her.
Use the Royal Shield to protect yourself.
But what foul magic could stand against the fabled Royal Shield? <hero_name> cut a path right to the warlock, ending her reign of terror.
You raise the mighty Royal Shield and block the storm, pushing towards the warlock and ending her life in a flash of steel.
The mountain was a formidable foe on its own, but the warlock's evil magic sweeps over you in a blanket of freezing air and bitter cold.
But the weather was unnaturally brutal, cutting through <hero_name>'s fur with ease. The warlock lay ahead, but could our hero make it?
A devilish warlock had blocked a nearby mountain pass, stranding countless innocents in a neverending blizzard. She had to be stopped!
A rogue warlock has blocked the pass over the mountains, stranding many of my friends in the cold. Please, go and save them!
The Blizzard of Hate
Slay the guards, then the feline tyrant.
Our hero tried in vain to slay the oppressors, but there were simply too many of them. Our hero was beaten, then thrown from the town.
You draw your blade, but the feline guards are quick to overpower you. They rough you up, then dump your still form outside the town gates.
Our hero's blade was quick and steady, slaying the feline oppressors with ease. The settlement was finally free of its tyrannical overlords.
Your sword is barely perceptible as it flashes from your side, through the guards. The tyrant falls just as quickly, and you leave a hero.
Go with the guards, then slay the tyrant.
Our hero decided to cut the head from the snake, slaying only the feline tyrant. The guards scattered, and the settlement was free at last.
When you are thrown before the feline tyrant, you reveal your intentions and slay him with ease. The guards escape, but the town is free.
Draw the moon scythe. Cut down these fools like wheat.
The Moon Scythe was enough to cause panic in the feline ranks, and our hero used it to full effect, freeing the settlement with their blood.
You heft the fabled scythe before you. None will survive. Panicking, the guards scatter, but many cannot escape the wide reach of the blade.
"There's more than one way to usurp a ruler..."\n
Thanks to the Spymaster's experience at lies and slander, the tyrant's reign is put to an end. The settlement is safe again.
Your Spymaster leads you to the settlement outskirts. It takes a while, but soon, rumours are spread that will end the tyrant's reign just as surely as steel.
"A fight? Let's go!"
The guards' skill at arms were no match for the Berserker's might. Within moments, the guards had routed, and the tyrant been usurped.
Your berserker leaps into battle. The guards scatter. While the berserker gives chase, you deal with the feline tyrant, nice and slow.
The moment you enter the town, the guards demand you kneel before the tyrannical ruler of the town and pledge your loyalty to them.
Upon entering the settlement, our hero was surrounded at once by feline guards, demanding he kneel before their lord.
<hero_name> had heard the tales of the wolf settlement -- and of its vicious feline oppressors. But what help could our hero provide?
Members of the Wolf Clan are being oppressed in this small town by feline tyrants. Save them, and their loyalty could be yours.
Judge, Jury, Executioner
Draw your blade and slay the beast!
Our hero's blade was quick, though not enough to fell the Rot-infested boar that attacked. Our hero was forced to flee with dire wounds.
You move to draw your weapon, but hesitate. The creature, some kind of Rot-infested boar, wounds you severely. You are forced to flee.
Our hero's blade was out in an instant, and the vile creature stood no chance against it. <hero_name> was well-rewarded for their bravery.
The beast, some kind of Rot-infested boar, puts up a tremendous fight before succumbing to your onslaught. The settlers reward you well.
Dive to the side -- evade the vile beast.
Our hero evaded the beast's charge, then chased the vile creature through the plains, forcing it from the land forever.
You leap to the side just as the strange creature attacks, avoiding its maw long enough to chase it free of the plains forever.
The Bane's Claw glimmers
The Bane's Claw sensed the creature's evil. it drew away the boar's strength, killing it. A powerful tool indeed.\n
A fearsome Rot boar bursts from the grass. As it spots the Bane's claw it begins to howl. Suddenly, it explodes, showering you with Rot.
Blast the creature with Wyld power!
The magic contained within the Wyldfyre Staff purged the charging beast, a Rot corrupted boar.
You hold the staff high. Its tip glows with arcane might. The beast shrinks back. You unleash the magic, purging the beast in white fire.
Hurry! Put on the Lionheart Breastplate.
The footsteps were the charge of a mighty Rot Boar. Though deadly, it could not pierce the Lionheart Breastplate, and was defeated.
Just as you tie the final strap, the creature attacks. Its tusks swipe by, but glance off your amour. You slay the beast.
Your quest has taken you to the heart of the plains, where wheat grows in thick forests of gold. Then you hear them: thundering footsteps...
Our hero's quest drew them to the very heart of the plains, lost in a forest of golden wheat. Then, from nowhere, thundering footsteps!
Word reached our hero of strange disappearances in a nearby plain. What evil could be lurking amongst these vast verdant seas?
Some of the plains settlers have been disappearing without reason. They're asking for a warrior to help get to the bottom of it.
The Lost
Call out the hound. Have him come to you.
Our hero tried to convince the hound to step out from the safety of the stones. Most offended, the hound stalked off in a huff.
Your tone irritates the hound. "I'm not yer servant, whelp. I don't know who you think you are, but here in Armello, you ain't nobody, yet."
Staying outside the stones, our hero summoned the hunter from afar. Far from being offended, the hunter rewarded them for their prudence.
You beckon to the old hound. He smirks, dropping a small parcel on the ground between you. "Smart to be wary. Don't forget that."
Step into the circle and confront the hunter.
Our hero was not shaken, however. The hunter was amused by <hero_name>'s show of bravado, but warned them to be more careful in future.
You march right into the stone circle. "Not wise to walk into a potential trap like that," the hound says. "You've got a lot to learn."
Demonstrate your Wyld Power
The figure in the circle was intimidated by the power of <hero_name>'s Wyld Talisman. He frantically apologised, fearing an attack.
You raise the talisman. The wolf will see your strength. He quickly apologises. "You're more powerful than I thought."
Reveal the Royal Banner
The figure was shamed into emerging by the King's authority, granted by the Royal Banner. Power commands respect.
You raise the Royal Banner. "Emerge stranger! The King demands it." Grudgingly the wolf exits. "Your influence reaches further than I knew."
"I know this hunter."
The doctor and the hunter appeared to be old comrades in arms! The hunter pledged loyalty to our hero, and offered a small token of respect.
"Deegan. Come out." The Stranger whispers. The hunter steps forward, head down. "If you've pledged your loyalty, then so shall I."
The hound leans against one of the standing stones. "Come on in!" he says, chuckling. But there is something off about how he says it...
The hunter was precisely where he said he would be, though something was off about the whole thing. <hero_name> was struck by unease.
A storied hunter of the Wolf Clan had requested a meeting with <hero_name>. The meeting's purpose, however, was a mystery.
I've heard there's a Wolf Clan hunter lurking about one of those odd stone circles nearby, and he's asking about you by name.
The Hunter in the Stones
Charge into the camp and slay the lot of them.
Throwing caution to the wind, our hero charged -- but boldness would not be rewarded that day, and <hero_name> fled with dire wounds.
You cut down the nearest bandit, but they quickly regroup. You flee after taking numerous wounds, and the magistrate is never seen again.
But the incredible odds did not deter our hero, who cut down the bandits with Wolf Clan steel. The magistrate was freed, the bandits slain.
You draw your blade and charge into the camp, slaying the lot of them. The grateful magistrate, offers you the aid of a loyal clan follower.
Cut a stealthy path to the magistrate.
Only through stealth would our hero succeed this day. Few bandits fell, but the magistrate was soon freed.
Deciding not to pick a fight, you creep along the perimeter of the cave, lowering the magistrate's cage and sneaking safely away.
Sharpen the Bane's Blade
The power of the Bane's Blade gave <hero_name> the strength to defeat every bandit. The fear in the magistrates eyes was oddly satisfying.
The bandits won't stand long. You walk into their camp, cutting the fools down. The magistrate begs for your mercy. It unsettles you.
"They need never see us."

In the camp, you find the magistrate hanging from a wicker cage suspended from the cave ceiling. Now how to deal with the bandits?

No doubt on orders from the mad king, a strong-willed Wolf Clan magistrate had been captured by bandits! Our hero rushed to save them.
A local magistrate loyal to the Wolf Clan has been captured by bandits! Rumor has it they've got a camp in the plains nearby...
The Hanging Judge
Stand tall! Challenge the shadow to reveal itself.

"This is not a shadow to fear, my friend. Allow me."

You accede to the Explorer, and watch as they summon the shadow forth. It is Vekkius, war hero of the Wolf Clan!
"Cover your eyes!"

"Break for shelter! Follow me!"

Half a generation ago, the Wolf Clan war hero, Vekkius, disappeared without a word. Were the rumors of him living in the mountains true?
I might've been seeing things, but while I was exploring the nearby mountains, I swear I saw Vekkius! You know, the old Wolf Clan war hero?
The Hermit
Ask the Wyld for advice.
Trying to commune with the Wyld, our hero instead seemed to anger the druids! The meeting ended in failure, and <hero_name> fled.

Standing outside the circle, you observe the figures and their odd rituals. You feel a stronger connection to the Wyld when they depart.

In the Standing Stones, looming before you, three robed figures hold court. Could these be the god-like druids of old?
<hero_name> approached the stone circle, the world fading into a haze. There, in the very center, the druids held court.
Our hero was in search of legends -- the ancient druids had been spotted nearby, and their ancient knowledge could prove useful.
I'm not one for gossip, but I've heard tales of ancient druids frequenting one of those strange stone circles dotting Armello.
Circle of Power
Ask the Wyld to halt the caravan.

A pinch of some strange powder causes a bright flash. One of the conjurer's parlour tricks. The caravan sees, and turns back.
"That caravan will stop soon!"

Get the Caravan's attention

There's an old circus seer traveling nearby with her caravan. You might want to meet her, maybe learn a thing or two about the future.
The Circus Caravan
Ask the Wyld for a distraction.

Word reached our hero of a hapless royal magus forced to flee the King's Guard. Perhaps this heretic could offer some useful information?
A royal magus is moving his scrolls through a nearby forest. His abilities seem to have angered the King's Guard. Could be a useful ally.
Mages and Scrolls
Draw steel! Fight!

Donning the garb of a farmer, you enter <quest_tile>. When the thieves spring their ambush, you're not surprised to see a band of treacherous rats!
<hero_name> drew the thieves in, posing as a helpless traveller. The supposed wolves were, in truth, a pack of cutthroat rats.
<hero_name> heard word of bandits flying the clan's crest during their sprees of murder and theft.
The Wolf Clan are naught but tyrants and thieves! Cutthroats fly your banner during their raids. Why do you allow this?
Honour the Clan
Throw a knife! Cut the rope!
Our hero failed to save the noble. The sound of the gallows creaking in the distance haunts <hero_name> to this day.

Attack!
Our hero forced back the executioners. The noble was safe, but <hero_name> was troubled by the blood spilt to save her.
The drafted militia of <quest_tile> are no match for a trained warrior. You free the noble, but are forced to wound many panicked guards.
Hurry! The Winged boots!

Barking protest, you step forward. The guards, hands forced, release the noble. It would seem that the law can be used to your advantage.

The dismal scene was to take place in <quest_tile>. <hero_name> arrived with only moments to spare!
A loyal advisor to the throne has been marked for execution. Her knowledge of the Mad King's ways might prove invaluable.
"Execution! The King's advisor is condemned to death. She will be hung by the neck until dead! "
Enemies Closer
Charge through the storm

Evacuate the surrounding area

"Stand back!"

Braving the storm, you struggle to the dungeon's mouth. A miasma of wind and rain spews forth from it in an endless stream.
The enchanted storm rose from the dungeon's maw. Without intervention, it would surely wreak havoc.
The sounds of a terrible storm echoes near our home. It's fury seems to be come from deep within <quest_tile>.
"Lighting crackles! It rises from underground!"

Take the bat to safety
<hero_name> forced the bat to return to safety. Overcome by his failure, the bat abandoned his quest, and fled.
The mountain is too perilous. You force the bat to accompany you down. Devastated, he leaves for home in the dead of night. Ashamed.

With the help of the explorer, our hero defeated the mountain. Preparation seem to be key in success.
With an explorer's help, the mountain offers no resistance. You find the travelers trapped in a cave. It would seem experience is useful.
Fire a flare

A search reveals the source of the rumours. A lone bat, hunting for signs of his companions, who vanished crossing the mountain range.
The creature, a lone bat, was scouring the mountain for any signs of his friends, who had been claimed by the mountain's deathly cold.
A terrifying beast was spotted prowling the mountain peaks of Armello.
"Monster! On <quest_tile>! Help!"
Strangers Abroad
Attack! Free the cub!
Deceived by the rats' underhanded trickery, <hero_name> was defeated, and the cub stolen away, never to be seen again.

<hero_name>'s legendary power brought the kidnappers down. The cub's village hailed him as their saviour. Perhaps soon, all of Armello would.
The rats are no match for you. They flee. The pup is safe. Inspired by your heroism, a member of the cub's village joins your cause.
Wait for nightfall

Well placed powders and crystal rocks caused an explosion that scattered the bandits. The alchemist's job done, our hero ran to free the cub.

Searching through the twisting trees, you spot the light of a campfire. The pup is tied to a post, surrounded by Rat Clan outlaws.
Through the forest thick, <hero_name> spied the pup. She was tied to a post, captured by a vicious rat pack.
A Wolf Clan cub had strayed from the clan grounds, searching for adventure. Since she entered <quest_tile>, none had heard from her.
"A Wolf Clan cub has been kidnapped! You must save her!"

Enter as a challenger

<hero_name> fought bravely, snatching victory and a prize from the other challengers.
None but the final warrior proves a challenge. After an hour of struggle, you claim victory from him, and are rewarded with a prize.

Watching the battle from afar, you remember much of the training you had forgotten. You leave treasureless, but ready for battle.

Protected by the Royal Shield, you enter without fear of injury. You avoid the risk of the final rounds, but win a lesser prize.
Bolstered by the Bane's Blade, challenge them all at once!
<hero_name> challenged each warrior at once. With the Bane's Blade in hand, no enemy could possibly survive.
In a stunning display of skill, you dismantle their onslaught. As you leave, they whisper your name. The blade feels good in your hand.
Arriving at the battleground you are met with the determined faces of a hundred warriors. This will be no easy test!
The tournament was filled with many aspiring challengers, all of whom were well versed in battle.
Word reached our hero of a tournament to be held in honour of the king's rise to the throne.
"Warriors! Prove yourselves! The Tournament is here!"
Champion's Prize

Draw steel. Death to traitors.

Arriving at the meeting grounds, you see a pack of wolves set up around a fire. They seem to be discussing if you have the subtlety to rule

Word reached <hero_name> that members of the Wolf Clan had planned a secret meeting without them. It was to take place at <quest_tile>.

Convince the mob to spare the village.

In the depths of the mire's waters, the thieves were revealed. A small village of toads, hidden in the fog.

<hero_name> tracked down the circus. The deer folk inside were odd after all. Perhaps they are behind the strange magic.
Strange magics have caused changes in the weather around <quest_tile>.  It's said that a mysterious deer circus is responsible.

Call strength from within. Break Free!
<hero_name> managed to defeat the beast, but was injured by its toxic Rot in the process.
The Bane struggles against you. You break its grip but not before the creature's beak has ripped into you, poisoning your soul.

Headbutt!
Protected by the Helm of Heroes, <hero_name> was able to defeat the Bane's attack and send it fleeing.

<hero_name> crept into <quest_tile>'s depths. The Moonhowlers were dead upon the stone. As <hero_name> saw them, a Bane sprung an ambush.
The Moonhowlers, brave Wolf Clan warriors, have not returned from hunting a bane that fled into <quest_tile>.
The Moonhowlers! Bravest warriors of the Wolf Clan. Champions of our clan, have vanished into the darkness."

Ride out the nightmare
Whatever wyld magics were causing the dreams dealt a blow to our hero. <hero_name> was left weakened, with a troubled mind.
